papers.title: Places in Interaction: The National Archaeological Park Project as an Integrated Approach to Public Archaeology in China
papers.abstract: The aim of this paper is to re-examine how concepts of public archaeology have been established and developed in varying social and political contexts in China, and how the recent national archaeological park project is structured as an important approach for improving public-archaeology relationships and promoting the public uses of archaeology. Since all archaeological activities in China are exclusively regulated by the state, all archaeological resources are administered for the benefit of the public. As such, concepts of public archaeology demonstrate the efforts of Chinese archaeologists to re-evaluate public-archaeology relationships and uses of archaeology through public engagement as well as archaeological communications with the public. The national archaeological park project was launched in 2006 to expand the practice of archaeology with the creation of archaeological communications, public space, and community-driven programmes. The project facilitates multiple perspectives on public archaeology practice through public education, community cohesion, re-creation of public space, and local economic development.

ai_analysis.title_ko: 상호작용하는 공간: 중국의 공공 고고학 통합 접근법으로서의 국가고고학공원 프로젝트
ai_analysis.abstract_ko: 이 논문의 목적은 중국의 다양한 사회적, 정치적 맥락에서 공공 고고학의 개념이 어떻게 정립되고 발전해왔으며, 최근 추진된 국가고고학공원 프로젝트가 공공과 고고학의 관계를 개선하고 고고학의 공공적 활용을 촉진하기 위한 중요한 접근 방식으로 어떻게 구조화되어 있는지 재검토하는 것이다. 중국의 모든 고고학 활동은 국가에 의해 독점적으로 규제되며, 모든 고고학 자원은 공공의 이익을 위해 관리된다. 따라서 공공 고고학의 개념은 대중 참여 및 고고학적 소통을 통해 공공과 고고학의 관계와 고고학의 활용 방식을 재평가하려는 중국 고고학자들의 노력을 보여준다. 국가고고학공원 프로젝트는 고고학적 소통, 공공 공간, 지역사회 주도 프로그램을 창출하여 고고학의 실천 영역을 확장하기 위해 2006년에 출범하였다. 이 프로젝트는 공공 교육, 지역사회 결속, 공공 공간의 재창조, 지역 경제 활성화를 통해 공공 고고학 실천에 대한 다양한 관점을 촉진한다.
summary_3lines: 중국의 국가고고학공원 프로젝트를 중심으로 공공 고고학의 개념과 발전 과정을 재검토하고 공공 활용 방식을 분석하고자 한다.
국가 주도의 고고학 자원 관리를 바탕으로 소통, 공공 공간 창출, 지역사회 주도 프로그램 등 다각적인 공공 고고학 실천 방안을 고찰했다.
고고학 공원을 통한 공공 교육, 지역사회 결속 및 지역 경제 활성화는 국립공원 내 문화자원 활용과 탐방객 소통 실무에 시사점을 제공한다.
ai_analysis.research_purpose: 이 연구는 중국의 사회정치적 맥락에서 공공 고고학의 개념이 형성된 과정을 살펴보고, 2006년 시작된 국가고고학공원 프로젝트가 공공과 고고학의 관계 개선 및 공공 자원 활용에 기여한 구조적 특징을 분석하는 것을 목적으로 한다. 이를 통해 공공 공간 조성, 지역사회 참여, 교육 프로그램 등이 고고학 실천에 미치는 영향을 다각도로 평가하고자 한다.
key_findings: 중국의 고고학 활동은 국가의 독점적 규제 아래 공공의 이익을 위해 관리되며 공공 고고학 개념 발전의 기반이 됨
2006년 도입된 국가고고학공원 프로젝트는 고고학적 소통, 공공 공간 조성, 지역사회 프로그램의 확장을 이끎
공공 교육, 지역사회 결속, 공간 재창조, 지역 경제 발전이 상호 연계되어 공공 고고학의 실효성을 높임
practical_applications: 국립공원 내 역사문화자원 및 고고학 유적지를 활용한 공공 탐방 프로그램 및 교육 콘텐츠 기획
유적지 주변 공간을 단순 보존을 넘어 지역주민과 탐방객이 소통할 수 있는 공공 공간으로 재조조성
지역사회 주민이 주도적으로 참여하는 문화자원 보전 및 지역 경제 연계형 탐방 프로그램 운영
ai_analysis.korea_np_applicability_reason: 한국 국립공원에도 다수의 역사문화 자원과 사찰 유적이 포함되어 있어 탐방객 교육 및 지역사회 연계 측면에서 적용 가능하나, 문화재보호법 등 별도 법령의 적용을 받는 자원이 많아 직접적인 고고학 공원 방식보다는 문화자원 해석 및 탐방 프로그램 설계에 제한적으로 응용할 수 있음
field_checklist: 공원 내 역사문화 자원 및 유적지 현황이 체계적으로 파악되어 있는가
탐방객을 위한 역사문화 자원 해설 및 교육 프로그램이 마련되어 있는가
유적지 주변 공간이 탐방객 휴식 및 소통을 위한 공공 공간으로 기능하고 있는가
지역사회 주민이 공원 내 문화자원 활용 및 프로그램 운영에 참여하고 있는가
문화자원 활용이 지역 경제 활성화에 기여할 수 있는 연계 방안이 검토되었는가
cautions: 국립공원 내 문화자원과 고고학 유적지는 문화재보호법 등 관련 법령에 따른 엄격한 규제를 받으므로 개발 및 공간 재조성 시 사전 협의가 필수적임
지역사회 주도 프로그램 운영 시 과도한 상업화나 생태계 훼손이 발생하지 않도록 철저한 모니터링이 필요함
recommended_followup_research: 국립공원 내 역사문화 자원 활용이 탐방객 만족도와 지역 경제에 미치는 영향 분석
자연보존과 문화유적 활용의 조화를 위한 국립공원 관리 거버넌스 구축 방안 연구

papers.title: Challenges and opportunities for monitoring wild Nile crocodiles with scute mark-recapture photography
papers.abstract: The global conservation status of Nile crocodiles (Crocodylus niloticus) was last assessed in 1996. The species presents particular difficulty in monitoring because it can be cryptic, require expertise to handle, and caudal tail tags and transmitters are often lost. Some studies advocate mark-recapture techniques based on photograph identification of the unique scute markings of crocodile tails as a non-invasive means of monitoring their populations. Researchers developed this method with crocodiles in captivity. In this study, we test the technique under field conditions by monitoring crocodiles from 2015 to 2017 in the Sunset Dam in the Kruger National Park. Using a Cormack-Jolly-Seber open population model, we found that the dam may host 15–30 individuals, but that there is a high turnover of individuals and much uncertainty in model outputs. The dam’s population thus has high rates of immigration and emigration. The method proved challenging under field conditions, as there was bias in identifying scute markings consistently. The efficient use of the method requires an exceptional quality of photographic equipment. Animal crypsis, however, remains an issue. In this study, we discuss how to improve the mark-recapture photography methodology, especially to adapt the technique for citizen science initiatives.Conservation implications: Using scute mark-recapture photography presents challenges under field conditions. These challenges require innovative, practical and analytical solutions to successfully use the technique before monitoring programmes, aimed at ensuring the persistence of crocodiles in the wild, can be implemented.

ai_analysis.title_ko: 비늘 표식 재포획 사진 기법을 활용한 야생 나일악어 모니터링의 도전 과제와 기회
ai_analysis.abstract_ko: 나일악어(Crocodylus niloticus)의 전 세계적 보전 상태는 1996년에 마지막으로 평가되었습니다. 이 종은 은폐성이 강하고 다루는 데 전문성이 요구되며 꼬리표나 발신기를 자주 잃어버리기 때문에 모니터링에 특별한 어려움이 있습니다. 일부 연구에서는 개체군 모니터링을 위한 비침습적 수단으로 악어 꼬리의 독특한 비늘 무늬를 사진으로 식별하는 표식 재포획 기법을 옹호합니다. 연구자들은 사육 상태의 악어를 대상으로 이 방법을 개발했습니다. 본 연구에서는 크루거 국립공원의 선셋 댐에서 2015년부터 2017년까지 악어를 모니터링하여 야외 조건에서 이 기술을 테스트했습니다. 개방형 개체군 모델인 Cormack-Jolly-Seber 모델을 사용한 결과, 이 댐에는 15~30마리의 개체가 서식할 수 있지만 개체 유출입이 많고 모델 결과의 불확실성이 크다는 점을 발견했습니다. 따라서 댐의 개체군은 높은 이입률과 이출률을 보입니다. 비늘 무늬를 일관되게 식별하는 데 편향이 존재했기 때문에 이 방법은 야외 조건에서 까다로운 것으로 입증되었습니다. 이 방법을 효율적으로 사용하려면 뛰어난 품질의 사진 장비가 필요합니다. 그러나 동물의 은폐성은 여전히 문제로 남아 있습니다. 본 연구에서는 표식 재포획 사진 촬영 방법론을 개선하는 방안, 특히 시민 과학 주도 프로그램에 이 기술을 맞춤 적용하는 방법에 대해 논의합니다. 보전적 시사점: 비늘 표식 재포획 사진 촬영은 야외 조건에서 과제를 안겨줍니다. 이러한 과제는 야생 악어의 지속 가능성을 보장하기 위한 모니터링 프로그램을 구현하기 전에 이 기술을 성공적으로 사용하기 위한 혁신적이고 실용적이며 분석적인 솔루션을 요구합니다.
summary_3lines: 악어 등 야생동물의 비침습적 개체군 모니터링을 위해 비늘 무늬 사진 식별(표식 재포획) 기법의 현장 적용 가능성을 검증하고자 하였다.
크루거 국립공원 현장 적용 결과, 개체의 높은 유출입과 은폐성, 무늬 식별 편향 등으로 인해 모니터링에 상당한 한계와 불확실성이 존재함을 확인하였다.
성공적인 현장 적용을 위해서는 고성능 촬영 장비 도입, 분석 모델의 고도화, 그리고 시민과학을 연계한 실용적 데이터 수집 체계 구축이 필수적이다.
ai_analysis.research_purpose: 본 연구는 기존에 사육 상태에서 개발된 비늘 무늬 사진 식별(표식 재포획) 기법을 실제 야외 환경에서 적용하여 그 실효성을 검증하고, 개체군 모니터링의 한계점과 개선 방안을 도출하는 것을 목적으로 합니다. 특히 현장 조건에서의 무늬 식별 편향, 높은 개체 유출입률, 장비 제약 등을 분석하여 향후 야생동물 모니터링 및 시민과학 프로그램에 적용할 수 있는 대안을 제시하고자 합니다.
key_findings: 선셋 댐의 나일악어 개체군은 약 15~30마리로 추정되나, 이입과 이출이 빈번하여 개체군 변동의 불확실성이 높았다.
야외 환경에서 악어의 은폐성과 비늘 무늬 식별 과정의 일관성 부족으로 인해 데이터 수집에 편향이 발생했다.
사진 기반 표식 재포획 기법의 효율적 운영을 위해서는 고성능의 전문 사진 장비와 정교한 개체군 분석 모델이 필수적이다.
practical_applications: 멸종위기 야생생물 모니터링 시 개체 식별 정확도를 높이기 위해 고해상도 카메라 및 장비 기준을 마련한다.
단순 육안 조사나 단발성 촬영을 넘어 개체군 유출입과 은폐성을 고려한 장기 개방형 개체군 모델을 적용한다.
현장 모니터링 인력 부족을 보완하기 위해 탐방객 및 자원봉사자가 참여하는 시민과학 기반 사진 제보 시스템을 기획한다.
ai_analysis.korea_np_applicability_reason: 한국 국립공원은 수달, 산양, 삵 등 특정 개체 식별이 필요한 멸종위기 야생생물 모니터링을 상시 수행하고 있어 사진 기반 표식 재포획(무늬·털 패턴 등) 기법의 응용 잠재력이 높으나, 대상 종의 생태적 특성이 달라 직접적인 현장 적용에는 맞춤형 보정이 필요합니다.
related_laws: 야생생물 보호 및 관리에 관한 법률 제19조
field_checklist: 개체 식별용 사진 촬영을 위한 고해상도 장비(망원렌즈 등)가 확보되었는가?
대상 개체의 신체적 특징(비늘, 반점, 털 패턴 등)을 일관되게 대조할 수 있는 기준 카탈로그가 있는가?
현장 조사 시 개체의 은폐성과 출현 환경(일조량, 은신처 등)에 따른 관찰 편향을 통제하고 있는가?
개체군 규모 산정을 위한 통계 모델(Cormack-Jolly-Seber 등) 적용 시 유출입 요인이 고려되었는가?
시민과학 연계 시 일반 탐방객이 촬영한 사진의 위치와 메타데이터가 정확히 검증되는가?
cautions: 현장 조건(빛 반사, 탁도, 은폐 등)에 따라 사진 식별률이 크게 좌우되므로 단일 방법만 의존하는 것은 주의해야 합니다.
개체 이동성이 높은 종의 경우 짧은 기간의 조사로는 정확한 개체군 추정이 어려우므로 예산과 일정 수립 시 장기 모니터링 계획을 반영해야 합니다.
recommended_followup_research: 인공지능(AI) 기반 이미지 자동 식별 알고리즘을 도입한 야생동물 개체 매칭 정확도 향상 연구
국내 주요 멸종위기종(수달 등)을 대상으로 한 사진 기반 비침습적 모니터링 프로토콜 개발 연구
ai_recommended_topics: Camera trap mark recapture wildlife monitoring

papers.title: An Integrated Approach of Landscape Design in the Rehabilitation of an Urban River Corridor: River Tinto
papers.abstract: Due to the increasing demand for its water resources, the changes in land use and the fast urban sprawl, the river Tinto became the mass of surface water of the river Douro´s watershed with lower physicochemical and biological quality. Taking into account its scale and urban context, the severity of the pollution level and the periodic flooding problem, became urgent to accomplish priority solutions for its riverside landscape, based on natural recovery principles and flood protection. The purpose of this paper is to stress the contribution of the integrated approach of landscape design in the improvement of the life quality and safety assurance of the local population, taking into account information and proposals from previous projects, plans and programmes, bioengineering technical knowledge and the national legal mechanisms related to water resources management. It was intended to rehabilitate a stretch of the river Tinto with the creation of a riverside urban park – Meiral Park. This project’s aim was to extend and qualify the public space, ensuring the river resilience and enhancing the hydraulic connectivity of its ecosystems and the multiple functionality of the place, through the integration of different uses – production, protection and recreation. With this project, it became obvious that landscape planners can take a more active and valid role in the management of water resources, through a multidisciplinary and intersectoral collaboration exercise. Indeed, it is believed that in the current political and economic context, incorporated into the guidelines of the Water Framework Directive, landscape design will gain a new dimension in the sustainable management of water resources.

ai_analysis.title_ko: 도시 하천 회랑 복원을 위한 조경의 통합적 접근: 틴토강 사례
ai_analysis.abstract_ko: 수자원 수요 증가, 토지 이용 변화, 급격한 도시 확산으로 인해 틴토강은 도루강 유역에서 물리화학적 및 생물학적 수질이 가장 낮은 지표수 수역이 되었습니다. 하천의 규모와 도시적 맥락, 오염 수준의 심각성, 주기적인 홍수 문제를 고려할 때, 자연 복원 원리와 홍수 방어에 기반한 강변 경관의 우선적 해결책을 마련하는 것이 시급해졌습니다. 본 논문의 목적은 이전 프로젝트, 계획 및 프로그램의 정보와 제안, 생태공학적 기술 지식, 수자원 관리와 관련된 국가 법적 메커니즘을 고려하여 지역 주민의 삶의 질 향상과 안전 보장에 조경의 통합적 접근이 기여하는 바를 강조하는 것입니다. 이는 강변 도시 공원인 메이랄 공원을 조성하여 틴토강의 특정 구간을 복원하는 것을 목표로 했습니다. 이 프로젝트의 목적은 생산, 보호, 휴양 등 다양한 용도의 통합을 통해 하천의 회복력을 보장하고 생태계의 수리적 연결성과 장소의 다기능성을 강화함으로써 공공 공간을 확장하고 자격을 갖추게 하는 것이었습니다. 이 프로젝트를 통해 조경가들이 다학제적이고 부문 간 협력 활동을 통해 수자원 관리에서 더 능동적이고 타당한 역할을 할 수 있음이 명백해졌습니다. 실제로 현재의 정치 및 경제적 맥락에서 물 기본 지침의 지침에 통합된 조경 디자인이 수자원의 지속 가능한 관리에서 새로운 차원을 얻을 것이라고 믿어집니다.
summary_3lines: 도시화로 오염되고 홍수 위험이 커진 틴토강 하천 회랑을 대상으로 자연 복원과 홍수 방어를 결합한 통합적 조경 계획 방안을 마련하고자 함.
과거 계획 자료, 생태공학 기술, 법적 제도를 융합하여 생산·보호·휴양이 공존하는 메이랄 수변공원을 조성하고 수리적 연결성과 생태계 회복력을 강화함.
수자원 관리와 도시 하천 복원 과정에서 조경 계획가와 다부서 간의 협력이 지속 가능한 생태계 관리에 핵심적인 역할을 함을 확인함.
ai_analysis.research_purpose: 본 연구는 급격한 도시화로 오염되고 훼손된 틴토강 하천 회랑을 대상으로, 생태공학 기술과 자연 복원 원리를 적용하여 수변 공간을 친환경적으로 복원하는 통합적 조경 설계 방안을 제시하는 것을 목적으로 합니다. 아울러 홍수 방어, 생태계 연결성 회복, 지역 주민의 삶의 질 향상을 동시에 달성할 수 있는 다기능적 수변 공원 조성 모델을 구축하고자 합니다.
key_findings: 생태공학적 기법을 적용한 수변공원 조성을 통해 하천의 수리적 연결성과 생태계 회복력을 동시에 증진함.
생산, 보호, 휴양 기능을 통합한 토지 이용 계획을 통해 단일 목적 하천 공간의 한계를 극복함.
다부서 간 협력과 통합적 조경 계획이 수자원 관리 및 도시 하천 복원의 실효성을 높이는 핵심 요인임을 증명함.
practical_applications: 국립공원 내 도심 인접 하천 및 수변 구역 복원 시 생태공학적 기법과 친환경 홍수 방어 시설을 도입한다.
탐방로, 휴식 공간, 생태 보호 구역이 공존할 수 있도록 다기능적 토지 이용 계획을 수립한다.
지자체 및 유관기관과의 다학제적 협력 거버넌스를 구축하여 수변 생태계 관리의 전문성을 높인다.
ai_analysis.korea_np_applicability_reason: 한국 국립공원 내에도 도심 인접 하천이나 탐방객 집중형 수변 구역이 존재하여 생태적 복원 및 친환경 재해 예방 기법을 일부 원용할 수 있으나, 본 논문은 도시 하천 및 도심 공원 조성을 주된 대상으로 하여 국립공원 전역보다는 공원 주변부나 도심형 국립공원 관리사무소의 수변 관리 업무에 더 직접적으로 부합함.
field_checklist: 하천 구역 내 물리화학적 수질 및 생물학적 건강성 지표가 사전에 조사되었는가
홍수 방어 구조물 설치 시 자연석, 식생 등 생태공학적 공법이 충분히 검토되었는가
수변 공간 내 탐방객 휴식 공간과 생태 보호 구역 간의 완충 공간이 확보되었는가
하천 생태계의 상하류 수리적 연결성을 저해하는 인공 구조물이 식별되었는가
유관기관 및 전문가가 참여하는 다부서 협력 체계가 마련되었는가
cautions: 국내 국립공원은 엄격한 자연공원법 규제를 받으므로 도시형 하천 공원 설계를 그대로 적용하기에는 법적 제약이 따를 수 있음.
대규모 수변 공원 조성 시 막대한 예산이 소요될 수 있으므로 국립공원 특성에 맞는 단계적 예산 집행 계획이 필요함.
recommended_followup_research: 국립공원 내 도심 인접 하천의 생태적 건강성과 탐방객 이용 압력 간의 상관관계 분석
한국 국립공원 특성을 반영한 친환경 하천 복원 및 재해 예방 통합 지침 개발 연구

papers.title: Transboundary Cooperation: The Best Way to Share Common Responsibility for Future
papers.abstract: The Bavarian Forest National Park (BFNP) and Šumava National Park (ŠNP), established in 1969 and 1991, respectively, are located between Prague and Munich. Their long common border accents the transboundary issue regarding nature conservation, ecological corridors and connectivity. Plans to protect this large forest landscape, dating back to the early twentieth century, were never implemented due to the two World Wars and Iron Curtain. Initially, there were many joint activities. Many common projects (e.g., joint information centre, transboundary public transport system, GPS lynx and deer telemetry) were conducted. Both sides have learned a lot during these 25 years of cooperation. The main obstacles in cooperation are economic differences between the regions, language barriers and different policies and laws. There is only one common ecosystem of mountain forests, common populations of lynx, capercaillie or bark beetle, and the partners have to learn how to share their common responsibility for the future. Step by step, the transboundary cooperation is improving, which is very important in good years, but maybe even more important in bad years. The principle stance of the transboundary partner can buffer threatening in the neighbouring national park and support recovery when the crisis is over.

ai_analysis.title_ko: 국경 초월 협력: 미래를 위한 공동 책임을 나누는 가장 좋은 방법
ai_analysis.abstract_ko: 1969년과 1991년에 각각 설립된 독일의 바이에른 숲 국립공원과 체코의 슈마바 국립공원은 프라하와 뮌헨 사이에 위치하고 있습니다. 두 공원의 긴 국경선은 자연보전, 생태 회랑, 연결성과 관련된 국경 초월적 이슈를 부각합니다. 20세기 초부터 이 거대한 산림 경관을 보호하려는 계획이 있었으나, 두 차례의 세계대전과 철의 장막으로 인해 이행되지 못했습니다. 초기에는 공동 정보 센터, 국경 초월 대중교통 시스템, GPS를 활용한 스페인스라소니와 사슴 텔레메트리 등 많은 공동 활동과 프로젝트가 진행되었습니다. 양측은 지난 25년간의 협력을 통해 많은 것을 배웠습니다. 협력의 주요 장애물은 지역 간 경제적 격차, 언어 장벽, 서로 다른 정책과 법률입니다. 산악림이라는 단 하나의 공동 생태계, 스페인스라소니, 뇌조, 나무좀 등의 공동 개체군이 존재하며, 파트너들은 미래를 위한 공동 책임을 나누는 법을 배워야 합니다. 국경 초월 협력은 단계적으로 개선되고 있으며, 이는 상황이 좋을 때도 매우 중요하지만 위기 상황일 때 아마도 훨씬 더 중요할 것입니다. 국경 초월 파트너의 원칙적인 태도는 인접 국립공원의 위협을 완화하고 위기가 끝난 후 회복을 지원할 수 있습니다.
summary_3lines: 인접한 두 국립공원이 단일 생태계 보호를 위해 국경을 초월한 협력 체계를 구축하고 운영해 온 25년간의 경험을 분석했습니다.
공동 모니터링과 인프라 구축 등 다양한 협력을 추진해 왔으나 경제적 격차와 제도적 차이가 주요 장애물로 작용함을 확인했습니다.
위기 상황 대응과 생태계 회복을 위해 인접 관리청 간의 지속적이고 원칙적인 협력 체계 구축이 필수적이라는 시사점을 도출했습니다.
ai_analysis.research_purpose: 본 연구는 인접 국가에 위치한 두 국립공원(바이에른 숲 국립공원과 슈마바 국립공원)의 25년간에 걸친 국경 초월 협력 사례를 분석하여, 단일 생태계 보호를 위한 공동 책임의 중요성과 협력 과정의 장애물 및 극복 방안을 도출하고자 합니다.
key_findings: 공동 정보 센터 운영, 대중교통 연계, 야생동물(스페인스라소니, 사슴) GPS 텔레메트리 등 다양한 공동 프로젝트를 성공적으로 수행함
협력의 주요 장애물로 지역 간 경제적 격차, 언어 장벽, 상이한 정책 및 법률 체계가 작용함
평상시뿐만 아니라 병해충 발생 등 위기 상황에서 인접 공원의 협력적 대응이 생태계 회복에 결정적 역할을 함
practical_applications: 인접한 국립공원 또는 보호지역 간 공동 생태계 모니터링 프로그램(야생동물 이동, 병해충 등)을 공동으로 기획하고 운영합니다.
행정구역 경계를 넘어선 탐방로 연계 및 대중교통 노선 확장을 통해 탐방객 편의를 도모합니다.
제도적·언어적 차이를 극복하기 위한 정기적인 실무자 협의체와 공동 위기 대응 매뉴얼을 마련합니다.
ai_analysis.korea_np_applicability_reason: 한국의 국립공원은 대부분 국가 내 행정구역 경계에 위치하여 국경 초월 이슈는 직접적이지 않으나, 지자체 경계를 넘나드는 광역 생태축(예: 백두대간) 관리 및 인접 보호지역 간 연계 관리에 유사한 거버넌스 원칙을 적용할 수 있습니다.
related_laws: 야생생물 보호 및 관리에 관한 법률 제4조
field_checklist: 인접 관리기관과의 정기 실무 협의회가 연 2회 이상 개최되고 있는가?
공동 생태계(야생동물 이동 등)에 대한 통합 모니터링 데이터가 공유되고 있는가?
병해충이나 산불 등 재난 발생 시 인접 기관과의 공동 대응 체계가 마련되어 있는가?
행정 경계를 연계하는 탐방로 및 안내 체계가 상호 호환되도록 구축되어 있는가?
기관 간 법령 및 제도 차이를 조율하기 위한 가이드라인이 존재하는가?
cautions: 국내 실정에 맞추어 적용할 때 지자체 간 이해관계 상충이나 예산 분담 문제 발생 가능성에 유의해야 합니다.
국가 간 협력 사례이므로 국내 지자체 간 또는 유관기관 간 협력 시에는 국내법 및 조례의 범위를 준수해야 합니다.
recommended_followup_research: 보호지역 간 경계 초월 협력이 생태계 건강성 회복에 미치는 정량적 효과 분석
행정구역 경계 지역의 보호지역 관리를 위한 통합 거버넌스 모델 개발 연구

papers.title: Foreword
papers.abstract: Literacy acquisition is a complex, multifaceted process that requires educational pedagogy that is beyond the purview of any single discipline. Collaboration among general and special education teachers, speech–language pathologists (SLPs), administrators, and families is essential to meet the reading and writing needs of all children most effectively, especially those at risk for or with identified language and learning impairments. Despite a growing philosophical consensus regarding the value of collaboration to promote literacy, teachers and SLPs too often work independently and focus largely on separate linguistic domains. Typically, teachers work in the classroom and provide instruction in written language, whereas SLPs primarily operate outside of the classroom, providing intervention to address the spoken language needs of students. In fact, a recent survey by the American Speech-Language-Hearing Association (2003) indicates that school-based SLPs spend an average of 20 hours each week using a pull-out approach and only 1 hour working in the classroom and 1 hour providing consultation. A number of reasons may account for the disparity between philosophical orientation and actual practice regarding collaboration, including (1) uncertainty about roles and responsibilities; (2) limited appreciation of the connections among language, literacy, and learning; (3) lack of professional preparation at the preservice or in-service level in designing and implementing collaborative partnership models of instruction and intervention; and (4) insufficient research demonstrating the efficacy of collaborative practices. To make meaningful changes in professional practice patterns and to more closely align philosophy and practice about literacy collaboration, several questions have to be addressed. What are the roles and responsibilities of different professionals over the course of a student's school day with respect to literacy education? Where do members of the education team gain content knowledge about spoken and written language and their interconnections? How do educators obtain the training necessary to form and maintain productive collaborative partnerships? How do educators find and preserve time for collaboration? How do educators gain administrative support and resources for time-intensive collaborative practices? What information would be most beneficial for SLPs and teachers to share with one another to help students become literate? How do educators operationalize joint responsibility in order to meet students' Individualized Education Program (IEP) goals? How can SLPs most effectively support the learning needs of students in the classroom environment? When is a collaborative model appropriate and when are other service delivery models preferable to meet the language and literacy needs of students? This issue of Topics in Language Disorders attempts to tackle these and other questions and focuses on ways that SLPs and teachers in general and special education can collaborate successfully in the provision of literacy-related services for students at risk for or with identified language impairments. The compilation of articles addresses guiding principles, challenges and solutions, and evidence-based practices for establishing and maintaining productive literacy partnerships between SLPs and teachers. Case profiles are used to provide a framework for meaningful collaboration in the areas of emergent literacy, word recognition, reading comprehension, written composition, and assistive technology. This issue was motivated by the work of the Council for Exceptional Children (CEC)/Division for Communicative Disabilities and Deafness (DCDD), Committee on Speech and Language Learning Disabilities in Children. The primary purpose of DCDD is to promote the welfare, development, and education of infants, toddlers, children, and youth with communication disabilities or who are deaf or hard of hearing. The Committee on Speech and Language Learning Disabilities in Children supports this work through its focus on the communication and learning needs of children and adolescents with speech, language, and learning disabilities. For the past several years, the committee has dedicated its efforts to encourage collaboration among school professionals to improve children's language and literacy development. In the first article, Paul, Blosser, and Jakubowitz put forth a set of guiding principles for successful literacy partnerships and propose possible solutions for many of the challenges encountered by teachers, SLPs, and other team members in the collaborative process. From the authors' perspective, adoption of these principles enables school professionals to take joint responsibility for selecting student goals and strategies consistent with curricular content and demands, preserving time for collaboration, making the literacy partnership a priority, establishing effective and ongoing communication systems, gaining administrative support, and participating in professional development experiences to prepare for and understand partners' roles and responsibilities. Paul, Blosser, and Jakubowitz remind us that embracing a partnership perspective does not preclude a direct service role for SLPs. Rather, the principles offer a framework for implementing collaborative services as appropriate to meet specific literacy needs of children in general and special education. In this regard, their article concludes with a Literacy Partnership Plan to assist teachers and SLPs in determining if, when, and how to implement a collaborative approach to literacy instruction and intervention. In the second article, Roth and Troia demonstrate how a collaborative philosophy can be applied to the emergent literacy and word-recognition needs of preschool children and children in early primary grades. The authors clearly demonstrate how language and literacy are connected, providing developmental information about spoken language skills that are associated with early literacy acquisition. They emphasize the value of collaboration for enhancing literacy development of all children, especially those at risk for or identified with language impairments or learning disabilities. Furthermore, they stress the importance of beginning collaborative efforts early in a child's school career. Roth and Troia provide specific examples of three partnership models for promoting emergent literacy and word recognition: demonstration lessons, team teaching, and consultation. The models highlight three practices that are critical to effective school-based service delivery: (1) developmentally appropriate, (2) classroom-based, and (3) consistent with an evidence-based paradigm. Readers will appreciate how this article on research-to-practice partnerships in emergent and early literacy supports national priorities for prevention and early identification of literacy deficits. The issue continues with Ehren's article, which highlights the particular challenges faced by SLPs who work with high-school students with reading comprehension problems. She explains that reading comprehension difficulties often occur because students have not become strategic readers; they do not use effective and efficient strategies for deriving meaning from printed text. From Ehren's perspective, high-school teachers need to recognize that reading comprehension difficulties may impede a student's ability to acquire subject content knowledge. Similarly, she stresses the need for SLPs to appreciate the importance of incorporating curricular content into their reading comprehension intervention programs. Because of the far-reaching effects of reading comprehension deficits, Ehren asserts that instruction and intervention in this area necessitate a collaborative approach among general education teachers, special education teachers, and SLPs to help students become strategic readers. Ehren shows how literacy partnerships can provide services that are responsive, intensive, and systematic, which she argues are the three main features of effective intervention for enhancing reading comprehension. Through her “before and after” case study, she demonstrates how a results-oriented and curriculum-relevant literacy partnership with these features can transform a student from a nonstrategic to a strategic reader. The focus shifts to literacy partnerships for improving writing composition in Nelson and Van Meter's article. They show how SLPs can partner with general and special education teachers in the use of an innovative writing lab approach. In this classroom-based model, literacy partners combine language instruction and intervention to address concurrently the written language composition needs of individual students. Continuous monitoring procedures permit partners to jointly modify initial objectives and document each student's growth over time. On the basis of their experience with the writing lab approach, they offer possible solutions to four challenges inherent in professional collaboration: gaining invitation into classrooms; establishing a shared routine through collaborative planning; creating opportunities to address individual goals; and negotiating theoretical perspectives and partner roles. Finally, Nelson and Van Meter show that benefits of their fully integrated instruction plus intervention model extend beyond written language composition to spoken communication, social interaction, and self-regulation. In the concluding article, Gillette delves into an area that may represent a novel pairing for some SLPs and teachers, that of assistive technology (AT) and literacy partnerships. She builds a case for collaboration as the key to providing quality AT services and making the general education curriculum more accessible for students with reading, writing, and spelling deficits. Although legislation mandates that AT services and devices be considered on IEPs for all students with identified disabilities, she argues that in actual practice IEP teams often address AT services only for students with the most severe communication disabilities. Gillette sees a critical need for teams to be involved at all stages of the assessment process: initial planning, implementation, and follow-up. She demonstrates how collaborative teams can work together to design effective AT technology assessment and intervention plans to augment students' literacy skills. Readers seeking guidance for conducting AT assessments for their students may find her discussion of the benefits and limitations of three different AT assessment frameworks to be particularly helpful. Gillette summarizes available evidence for the use of AT to improve reading, writing, and spelling skills and guides the reader through each stage of the collaborative process by interweaving examples from her case study throughout the article. We hope the information in this issue helps you answer the questions we posed about establishing successful literacy partnerships and leads to many productive collaborative relationships that support our shared vision of enhancing student literacy. Froma P. Roth, PhD, CCC-SLP, Issue Editor Associate Professor, Department of Hearing and Speech Sciences, University of Maryland, College Park, College Park, Maryland Diane R. Paul, PhD, CCC-SLP, Issue Editor Director, Clinical Issues in Speech–Language Pathology, American Speech-Language-Hearing Association, Rockville, Maryland

ai_analysis.title_ko: 서론: 언어장애 분야
ai_analysis.abstract_ko: 문해력 습득은 단일 학문의 범위를 넘어서는 교육적 교수법이 요구되는 복잡하고 다면적 과정이다. 일반 및 특수 교육 교사, 언어치료사(SLP), 행정가, 가족 간의 협력은 모든 아동, 특히 언어 및 학습 장애 위험이 있거나 진단받은 아동의 읽기 및 쓰기 요구를 가장 효과적으로 충족하는 데 필수적이다. 문해력 증진을 위한 협력의 가치에 대한 철학적 공감대가 커지고 있음에도 불구하고, 교사와 언어치료사는 종종 독립적으로 일하며 별개의 언어 영역에 주로 집중한다. 전형적으로 교사는 교실에서 근무하며 문어 지도를 제공하는 반면, 언어치료사는 주로 교실 외부에서 활동하며 학생들의 구어 요구를 해결하기 위한 중재를 제공한다. 실제로 미국언어청각협회(2003)의 최근 조사에 따르면, 학교 기반 언어치료사는 매주 평균 20시간을 분리 교육 방식으로 보내고, 교실 내 근무는 단 1시간, 상담 제공은 단 1시간에 불과한 것으로 나타났다. 철학적 지향과 실제 협력 관행 사이의 이러한 격차는 (1) 역할과 책임에 대한 불확실성, (2) 언어, 문해력, 학습 간 연계성에 대한 제한적인 인식, (3) 협력적 파트너십 교수 및 중재 모델 설계·구현에 대한 사전/현직 전문 교육 부족, (4) 협력 관행의 효과성을 입증하는 연구 부족 등 여러 이유로 설명될 수 있다. 전문적 관행 패턴에 의미 있는 변화를 가져오고 문해력 협력에 대한 철학과 실제를 더 긴밀하게 조화시키기 위해 여러 질문들이 다뤄져야 한다. 문해 교육과 관련하여 학생의 학교생활 전반에 걸쳐 다양한 전문가의 역할과 책임은 무엇인가? 교육 팀 구성원은 구어 및 문어와 그 상호 연계성에 대한 내용 지식을 어디서 얻는가? 교육자들은 생산적인 협력 파트너십을 형성하고 유지하는 데 필요한 교육을 어떻게 받는가? 교육자들은 협력을 위한 시간을 어떻게 찾고 유지하는가? 교육자들은 시간 집약적인 협력 관행을 위해 행정적 지원과 자원을 어떻게 확보하는가? 학생들이 문해력을 갖추도록 돕기 위해 언어치료사와 교사가 서로 공유하는 데 가장 유익한 정보는 무엇인가? 교육자들은 학생들의 개별화된 교육 프로그램(IEP) 목표를 달성하기 위해 공동 책임을 어떻게 운영하는가? 언어치료사는 교실 환경에서 학생들의 학습 요구를 가장 효과적으로 지원할 수 있는가? 학생들의 언어 및 문해력 요구를 충족하기 위해 협력 모델이 적절한 시기와 다른 서비스 전달 모델이 선호되는 시기는 언제인가? 본 'Topics in Language Disorders' 호는 이러한 질문들과 기타 질문들을 다루며, 언어치료사와 일반 교사들이 협력하는 방안에 초점을 맞춘다.
summary_3lines: 국립공원 현장에서도 다양한 부서와 전문가 간의 협업이 필수적이나, 실제 현장에서는 부서별 칸막이 행정과 독립적 업무 수행이 고착화되어 있다.
역할 모호성, 교육 부족, 소통 부재 등으로 인해 철학적 공감대와 현장 실행력 사이에 큰 격차가 존재한다.
부서 간 명확한 역할 분담, 정기적인 정보 공유 체계 구축, 현장 중심의 실무 협업 모델 도입이 시급하다.
ai_analysis.research_purpose: 국립공원 탐방객 서비스 및 자원 관리 등 복합적인 현안을 해결하기 위해 다양한 분야의 전문가와 부서 간 협업의 중요성을 짚어보고, 실제 현장에서 협업이 원활히 이루어지지 않는 원인과 이를 극복하기 위한 실무적 과제를 도출하는 데 목적이 있다.
key_findings: 협력의 필요성에 대한 공감대는 높으나, 실제 현장 업무는 부서별·분야별로 엄격히 분리되어 수행됨.
역할과 책임의 불확실성, 전문 교육 부재, 협업을 위한 시간 및 행정 지원 부족이 주요 장애물로 작용함.
성공적인 현장 현안 해결을 위해서는 명확한 역할 정의와 지속적인 정보 공유, 제도적 뒷받침이 필수적임.
practical_applications: 탐방객 안전 및 자원 보호 복합 민원 발생 시, 관련 부서(탐방시설과, 자원보전과 등)가 참여하는 합동 태스크포스(TF)를 상시 운영한다.
신규 직원 교육 및 직장 내 교육(In-service) 시 타 부서의 주요 업무와 연계 지점을 이해할 수 있는 순환 근무 및 합동 워크숍을 확대한다.
부서 간 협업 성과를 평가하고 지원할 수 있는 행정적 인센티브와 정례 회의 체계를 마련한다.
ai_analysis.korea_np_applicability_reason: 본 논문은 교육 및 언어치료 분야를 다루고 있으나, 그 핵심 방법론인 '부서 간 칸막이 제거 및 다학제적 협업'은 국립공원 현장에서 탐방객 관리, 생태계 복원, 재난 대응 등 복합 행정 수요를 처리할 때 그대로 응용할 수 있기 때문이다.
field_checklist: 타 부서와의 협업이 필요한 현안 발생 시 공식적인 합동 회의가 개최되었는가?
업무 수행 시 관련 타 부서의 역할과 책임 범주가 명확히 공유되었는가?
현장 실무자들을 위한 부서 간 합동 교육 프로그램이 운영되고 있는가?
협업 업무 수행을 위한 충분한 시간과 행정적 자원이 배정되었는가?
부서 간 협업을 저해하는 제도적·절차적 장애 요인이 점검되었는가?
cautions: 부서 간 업무 영역이 모호해질 경우 책임 전가나 갈등이 발생할 수 있으므로 사전 역할 정립이 필수적이다.
협업에 소요되는 시간과 행정 비용이 과도하게 발생하지 않도록 효율적인 회의 및 보고 체계를 갖추어야 한다.
recommended_followup_research: 국립공원 내 부서 간 협업 저해 요인 분석 및 실무 개선 모델 개발 연구
탐방객 서비스 및 자원 관리를 위한 통합적 행정 거버넌스 구축 방안

papers.title: Public Health 4.0: Creating Health for Longer Lives
papers.abstract: The United States added 30 years to human life expectancy since 1900, an unprecedented achievement (Frieden, 2015). Many gains in human life expectancy since 1900 resulted from interventions affecting all people, such as reduction in air and water pollution, improved food and water safety, and better control of infectious diseases. In recent years, however, lifespan gains in the United States have reversed, influenced by declines in life expectancy among subpopulations, such as those with less than a high school education (National Research Council and Committee on Population, 2013), and the number of years people are living with ill health, a “decompression of morbidity” (Rowe & Berkman, 2022). This decreasing health span (years in good health) has occurred as an emerging body of evidence suggests that improved population health is possible, even into the oldest ages (Langa, 2015). Democratizing good health and function for all across the life course and at older ages would be a game changer for the future of the United States. In 2018, the National Academy of Medicine (NAM) identified healthy longevity as the leading grand challenge for the world. Healthy longevity is defined as “the state in which years in good health approach the biological life span, with physical, cognitive, and social functioning that enables well-being across populations” (National Academy of Medicine [NAM], 2022, p.1). NAM empaneled a Global Commission to create the Global Roadmap for Healthy Longevity (Global Roadmap; NAM, 2022). We contributed to the development of the Global Roadmap as Commission Co-Chair, Commissioners, and Study Director. The Global Roadmap emphasized that health is defined by the physical environment, social structures, education and work, and population-level public health interventions that influence the underlying biological mechanisms of aging that lead to chronic conditions, loss of functioning, and frailty in later life. The medical care system has an important role in healthy longevity across the life course in maintaining health and function in later years, but its impact on health is dwarfed by the factors addressed by public health. Based on findings and conclusions (Table 1), the commission recommended an emphasis on public health as a means to create a future that optimizes the well being of an aging population. We conclude that the United States can create healthy longevity for longer lives by resourcing and supporting public health systems and policies that build and maintain the health and capabilities of people at every age and stage of life. Global Roadmap for Healthy Longevity Findings, Conclusions, and Recommendations (NAM, 2022) Global Roadmap for Healthy Longevity Findings, Conclusions, and Recommendations (NAM, 2022) The United States needs to focus on actions that can eliminate disparities in lifespan and increase the health span (years in good health) for all. Achieving this will require redesigns across health sectors (public health, medical care, long-term care, social services) and integrating approaches to transforming education, physical environments, and work so these organizations support aging individuals and their well being and contributions. This transformation could create a virtuous cycle of health and prosperity for all ages, as shown in Figure 1 (NAM, 2022). The virtuous cycle of healthy longevity (NAM, 2022). Public health is “what we do as a society to ensure the conditions in which everyone can be healthy” (DeSalvo et al., 2017). According to NAM, “Public health systems are the single most powerful structure for tackling chronic conditions and equitably improving population health” (NAM, 2022, p. 182). However, the federal government has decreased its investments in public health since the early 1970s (Maani & Galea, 2020), constraining the opportunity to evolve to meet emerging needs and opportunities. This contrasts with peer countries, which have maintained their public health spending (Kamal & Hudman, 2020). We need new levels of investment to achieve equitable healthy longevity in the twenty-first century. According to the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), public health has three primary responsibilities: assessment, assurance, and policy and practice development (U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention [CDC], 2023). Subcomponents include assuring a competent workforce; informing, educating, and empowering; and providing or enabling conditions in every community to improve the opportunity for health and prevent disease, disability, and injury. Many countries include primary care as a component of their public health systems, but in the United States, primary care is categorized as part of the medical care system. United States public health systems use a range of tools to fulfill their responsibilities, from data collection and monitoring to policies and community-based programs. However, new strategies and tools at all levels and system redesign and reinvestment will be needed to deliver the conditions for healthy longevity, which would solve the increasing ill health of people of all ages, from the heartland to the coasts (NAM, 2022; Woolf & Aron, 2013). As we emerge from the coronavirus disease-2019 (COVID-19) pandemic, experts have offered proposals for public health system modernization. These encompass actions that are necessary but not sufficient to ensure a long-lived and healthier population. Examples include recommendations to modernize and standardize data capabilities and unify the public health system across all levels, including the CDC and state, local, tribal, and territorial health departments to improve the health return on investment (Bipartisan Policy Center, 2021). Recognizing the importance of social determinants of health, recent work has proposed that the United States design a Public Health system 3.0 in which local health departments or public health experts serve as “community health strategists” to inform and guide cross-sector collaboration on community resources, such as housing, access to food, and safety that deeply affect health (DeSalvo et al., 2017). If these and other programs addressing current health challenges were extended to include older adults, it would offer a foundation of health for all. Given that half the population is already in the second half of life (US. Census Bureau, 2023), new age-specific public health strategies are also needed to enable older people to experience increases in health span and healthy longevity (De Biasi et al., 2020). The health status of older people is shaped by the impact of advantage or disadvantage across their lives, but health and functioning can continue to be maintained or improved into the oldest ages (NAM, 2022). Improving the health and functioning of older people will enable them to live the lives they desire with meaning, dignity, and purpose (World Health Organization [WHO], 2015). Neglecting their needs will undermine the potential for extended health span for all and the return on investment from healthy longevity. Older people’s health must therefore be explicitly added to public health system responsibilities (NAM, 2022). The Global Roadmap provides a mandate to public health to build appropriate programs for each age group to promote health, function, and well-being and prevent and manage chronic conditions across the full life course (NAM, 2022). Primary prevention (prevention of a condition from developing) that addresses nutrition, physical activity, stress management, sleep, and substance use along with vaccines to prevent infectious disease and other health promoting conditions across communities can benefit people of all ages and stages. But different phases of life need tailored goals and approaches (De Biasi et al., 2020; WHO, 2015). Children and adolescents need a focus on child development, education, nutrition and physical activity, nurturing environments, social skills, and the best possible base of physical, cognitive, and emotional capacities for later life. Healthy adults without chronic conditions and preserved functioning need to build and continue healthy habits to maintain their health, obtain screening and early intervention for chronic conditions, and live in health-supporting environments that make healthy behaviors an easy option (Frieden, 2010). Although more can be done and investment varies widely by geography, public health has well-established agendas and strategies for health promotion in these populations (DeSalvo et al., 2019). Primary prevention has benefited older people in two ways: by improving their health as they reach later years and preventing serious illness in older people. For example, COVID-19 vaccinations were critical for older people, who were at high risk of hospitalization and death if they were infected and unvaccinated. Yet public health systems have focused little on designing effective primary prevention and health promotion programs tailored to the needs of older people. For example, ageism affects the health of older people, but it is not on the public health agenda. Similarly, nutrition, exercise, and sleep requirements change as people age, but health promotion messaging tailored to older people is not prioritized. Causes of loneliness or risk factors for chronic diseases vary by age group. Opportunities for social engagement are designed by older adults, and if well designed, improve health or prevent declines. Although primary prevention remains important, secondary (e.g. screening and contact tracing to detect and treat disease early and minimize its effects) and tertiary (e.g. managing age-related decline and the effects of chronic conditions) prevention is central to maintaining health in older populations. The majority of adults over the age of 65 experience multiple chronic conditions or age-related declines in capacity (St Sauver et al., 2015) and many face other challenges, such as loneliness and isolation (National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine, 2020). At this point in the life course, the goals of public health and medical care are to maintain functional capacity, manage the effects of chronic conditions, and prevent disease, disability, and geriatric syndromes such as falls, incontinence, delirium, and frailty, and the threats to psychological well-being rise in importance. Examples of community-based secondary prevention programs include programs to support knowledge of how to manage chronic conditions and minimize their functional consequences along with programs to decrease risk factors. Future opportunities for public health system programs should be expanded to tertiary prevention of the consequences of functional decline, such as environmental interventions that can help people adapt to losses of physical and cognitive capacity or provide home-based support for basic self-care needs. This can be integrated with long-term care systems needed for older adults who experience significant losses of physical or cognitive capacity and require ongoing care and support delivered in the homes, communities, and institutions by health care providers, optimally with adequate training in geriatric care. A public health system that delivers life course health promotion and prevention for all age groups, including older populations, will create healthy futures for all. This will require five components above and beyond the well-established public health functions. Lengthening health span and compressing periods of chronic ill health to the end of the lifespan (compression of morbidity) requires effective public health-led programs delivered at the community, city or county, state, and national levels. Initiatives need to use evidence for effective prevention, be relevant to health needs and drivers in each community, and be multidimensional, tailored to age and stage of life, and coordinated and integrated across all levels of government and sectors that affect health. Programs should target shared risk factors for multiple health outcomes, including improving health behaviors such as physical activity, nutrition, and sleep; stress reduction; preventing obesity, disability, smoking, and addiction; and promoting social connection and engagement to prevent loneliness and improve well being (De Biasi et al., 2020). To delay onset and minimize consequences of chronic conditions as long as possible, public health programs must go beyond health behaviors and support food security; nurturing and parenting; the conditions of the physical and built environment, including pollution; social conditions within communities; housing; and violence prevention. Air pollution reduction is an example of a population-based public health intervention that improves health for people of all ages. It is associated with 7 million deaths annually (WHO, 2023) and causes compromised neurocognitive development in children and dementia in older people (Cipriani et al., 2018). Similarly, safe and accessible sidewalks and parks have health benefits for older and younger people alike (NAM, 2022). Lengthening health span and compressing periods of chronic ill health to the end of the lifespan (compression of morbidity) requires effective public health-led programs delivered at the community, city, county, state, and national levels. As noted above, many primary prevention and health promotion efforts are important to older people. However, given the heterogeneity of health status among older people, preventive interventions should be tailored to subgroups of older people at different levels of risk (WHO, 2015). For healthy older people, the primary goal of age-appropriate public health interventions should be to prevent or delay the onset of chronic conditions, geriatric syndromes, and functional decline and loneliness while supporting resilience. This requires programs to resolve pervasive ageist attitudes that minimize the import of prevention and health promotion in older age. For those without chronic conditions, frailty, or functional decline, the goal is to prevent these. For those with such conditions, the goal is to preserve functioning by slowing disease and aging progression and managing the impacts of chronic conditions and prevent further declines and frailty. For those with advanced chronic conditions and impaired functioning, the goal is to maintain functioning, slow further declines, and support their ability to live their lives with meaning, dignity, and purpose in the setting of their choice. Public health systems, along with medical care and long-term care, failed this population during the COVID-19 pandemic. To meet these goals, a range of strategies and interventions is needed, including modernized data systems that capture granular data about older people’s health and function and risks; multidimensional community-based programs and policies to promote health for older people while diminishing ageist assumptions; integration and alignment among public health, medical care, and long-term care and social service systems; and redesigned long-term care systems. A new repertoire of community-based public health programs could support mental health and resiliency in aging, prevent loneliness, enable engagement, train and support family caregivers (e.g., care provision skills and self-care), and protect those with chronic disease, frailty, cognitive decline, or disability during emergencies. A new contingent of community health workers trained in public health and geriatrics precepts deployed by health departments could help to accomplish these goals. An initial stage for this work has been created in the Age-Friendly Public Health program, which is led by Trust for America’s Health, with the support of the John A. Hartford Foundation. The Age Friendly Public Health program brings new attention to the needs of older people within public health systems because “public health agencies rarely have dedicated funding or initiatives targeting adults 65 and older” (De Biasi et al., 2020, p. 3). The program’s goals are “promoting health, preventing disease, injury and frailty, and managing chronic conditions; optimizing physical, cognitive and mental health; and facilitating social and civic engagement” (De Biasi et al., 2020, p. 4). The program’s framework focuses on the role of the public health system to create the social and environmental conditions in communities to support the “6 Cs for healthy aging” (Trust for America’s Health, 2023): Connecting and convening multisector stakeholders; Coordinating existing supports and services; Collecting, analyzing, and translating relevant data; Communicating important public health information; Complementing existing health promoting programs; Creating and leading policy, systems, and environmental changes. The program has formed a network that includes federal government agencies and states, but it requires policy uptake, content expansion to match the evidence as to the many opportunities for health promotion for older adults, and amplified funding to have the impact needed for every community. Public health systems at the local, state, tribal, and territorial levels could foster the engagement of older people in public health in various paid and volunteer roles. For example, they could create a role for older adults as community health workers delivering community-level public health programs or serving as block captains in emergencies to reach those who are homebound. Well-designed roles would also maintain or improve the health of older workers. Older adults can be trained, for example, to educate children about how to manage asthma for themselves or family members (Reddy et al., 2007), and there is reason to believe that such training could improve older adults’ management of their own illness and overall health and well-being. Older community health workers could also deliver programs for older adults and intergenerational groups to the benefit of all involved. Public Health can also work across settings and disciplines to design and deploy paid or volunteer roles that improve health in the community and to seed effective organizations for connection and engagement among older adults and across generations, potentially in collaboration with community-based organizations or departments for the aging. An example of a volunteer program designed for such a win–win situation is the Experience Corps. This evidence-based program provides roles for older volunteers supporting the academic success of children in public elementary schools and thus building structural social capital (Carlson & Rebok, 2019; Fried et al., 2004; Rebok et al., 2019). ai_analysis.title_ko: 공중보건 4.0: 더 오래 건강한 삶을 위한 건강 창출
ai_analysis.abstract_ko: 미국은 1900년 이후 기대수명이 30년 이상 증가하는 전례 없는 성과를 거두었으나, 최근 교육 수준 등에 따른 계층별 기대수명 감소와 유병 기간 증가로 인해 건강 수명이 줄어드는 현상이 나타나고 있다. 모든 연령층에서 건강과 기능을 민주화하는 것은 미국의 미래를 바꿀 게임 체인저가 될 수 있으며, 2018년 미국 의학한림원(NAM)은 건강한 장수를 세계의 주요 과제로 지정하였다. NAM이 구성한 글로벌 위원회는 건강한 장수가 신체적, 인지적, 사회적 기능을 유지하여 전 생애에 걸쳐 웰빙을 가능하게 하는 상태라고 정의하며 건강한 장수를 위한 글로벌 로드맵을 발표했다. 이 로드맵은 물리적 환경, 사회적 구조, 교육 및 일자리, 그리고 공중보건 중재가 노화의 생물학적 메커니즘에 영향을 미쳐 만성 질환과 허약함을 예방하는 핵심 요인임을 강조한다. 의료 체계도 중요하지만 공중보건이 다루는 환경적·사회적 요인의 영향력이 훨씬 크며, 따라서 고령화 사회의 웰빙을 최적화하기 위해서는 공중보건 시스템과 정책에 대한 자원 지원이 필수적이다.
summary_3lines: 노령 인구의 증가와 함께 감소하는 건강 수명을 연장하기 위해 공중보건 중심의 전 생애 건강 관리 체계 구축 방안을 고찰함.
물리적 환경과 사회적 구조 등 공중보건적 개입이 노화와 만성 질환 예방에 의료 서비스보다 더 큰 영향을 미친다는 점을 확인무함.
고령화 사회에 대응하여 공원 환경을 활용한 건강증진 프로그램 및 공중보건 인프라 연계 정책을 강화할 필요가 있음.
ai_analysis.research_purpose: 본 연구는 미국을 중심으로 1900년 이후 기대수명 증가의 정체 및 건강 수명 단축 문제를 진단하고, 이를 해결하기 위한 공중보건 중심의 '건강한 장수(Healthy Longevity)' 달성 전략과 글로벌 로드맵의 주요 내용을 제시하는 것을 목적으로 한다.
key_findings: 1900년 이후 기대수명이 크게 증가했으나, 최근 소외 계층을 중심으로 기대수명이 감소하고 유병 기간이 늘어나는 추세가 나타남.
의료 치료 체계보다 물리적 환경, 사회적 구조, 공중보건 중재 등 외부 환경 요인이 개인의 건강 수명에 미치는 영향이 훨씬 큼.
미국 의학한림원(NAM) 글로벌 로드맵은 전 생애에 걸쳐 신체적·인지적·사회적 기능을 유지하는 '건강한 장수'를 핵심 과제로 제시함.
practical_applications: 국립공원 내 고령층 및 취약계층을 위한 무장애 탐방로와 치유의 숲 프로그램을 확대하여 건강 수명 연장에 기여한다.
보건복지부 및 지자체 보건소와 협력하여 국립공원 자연환경을 활용한 대국민 건강증진 및 만성질환 예방 프로그램을 공동 운영한다.
탐방객의 신체적·정신적 웰빙을 측정할 수 있는 공원 기반의 공중보건 모니터링 지표를 개발하고 현장 관리에 도입한다.
ai_analysis.korea_np_applicability_reason: 국립공원은 국민의 신체적·정신적 건강증진을 위한 천혜의 자연 자원이자 공중보건 공간이나, 논문 자체가 직접적인 공원 관리보다는 미국의 거시적 보건 정책을 다루고 있어 현장 적용에는 간접적 연계가 필요함.
field_checklist: 고령 탐방객을 위한 무장애 탐방로 및 편의시설이 적절히 배치되어 있는가
국립공원 내 자연 치유 및 건강증진 프로그램이 정기적으로 운영되는가
탐방객의 응급 상황 대처 및 안전을 위한 보건 의료 연계 체계가 구축되어 있는가
취약계층의 공원 접근성을 높이기 위한 지원 프로그램이 마련되어 있는가
탐방객의 신체 활동 및 웰빙 효과를 측정·평가하는 수단이 있는가
cautions: 국립공원 관리공단의 고유 임무인 자원 보전과 탐방객 건강증진 서비스 제공 간의 적절한 균형 유지 필요
의료 및 보건 분야와의 협력 사업 추진 시 예산 및 법적 근거 마련의 제약 고려
recommended_followup_research: 국립공원 자연환경 방문이 고령층의 건강 수명 연장에 미치는 정량적 효과 분석 연구
국립공원 자원을 활용한 공공 보건 의료 연계 프로그램 표준화 방안 연구

papers.title: Promoting Intergenerational Strategies: The Role of the Corporation for National Service
papers.abstract: A catalyst for corporations, foundations, and community groups. The United States has always relied on the generosity and commitment of its citizens to meet its challenges. Today millions of Americans volunteer every day, tutoring children, helping communities recover from natural disasters, restoring parks, and doing many other things to improve lives and bring people together. Tapping citizen power will be even more important as we enter a new century and a new era of limited government. Just because government is being reduced, it does not mean our problems are going away. Indeed, many of the problems facing our nation-from crime and drugs to illiteracy and homelessness-- are mounting. To meet these challenges, we need to unleash the greatest power our country has-the energy and idealism of our people. Above all, we must tap the power of 6o million Americans over age 55, who bring to what no other age group can-a lifetime of skills and experience as workers, parents, grandparents, and citizens. The Corporation for National Service, through the programs of the National Senior Service Corps, Learn and Serve America, and AmeriCorps, is working with thousands of nonprofit partners to strengthen the voluntary sector and unleash citizen power. Created in I993 with bipartisan support from Congress, the president, and community groups nationwide, the corporation now engages more than a million Americans in results-driven service. Our mission is to provide opportunities for Americans of all ages and backgrounds to engage in that addresses the nation's educational, public safety, environmental, and other human needs to achieve direct and demonstrable results and to encourage all Americans to engage in such service (U.S. Congress, I993). Taken together, the corporation's programs constitute an extensive structure that can help intergenerational approaches expand and flourish. To generate citizen on the scale needed, the corporation and its programs are designed as a catalyst for unleashing action from corporations, foundations, and community groups. By its very design, such is intergenerational. Service provides an avenue for people of all ages to contribute, strengthens ties among diverse individuals and groups, and expands individual definitions of citizenship and responsibility. Reciprocity, a central tenant of intergenerational activities, is present and reinforced in national programs across the country. People of all ages are potential givers and receivers of service. In the majority of cases, there is a direct reciprocal exchange among the primary constituencies, such as young people providing companionship and doing chores for older adults, while at the same time discovering the benefits of learning from their elders. Older people in the Foster Grandparents program, for example, tutor children in reading, comfort hospitalized children, help adolescent mothers learn parenting skills, and encourage incarcerated young offenders to get their lives back on track. In return, Foster Grandparents report that they receive as much as they give, in the form of new purposes in later life, new skills, and new opportunities to contribute to the wellbeing of individual children and young people. A less well-known but promising intergenerational model encourages young and old participants to serve side by side to address unmet needs in their communities. For example, participants may join forces to prepare meals in a homeless shelter, adopt and clean up a riverbed, or coordinate a book drive for early readers in poorly funded schools. Service becomes both a vehicle and a catalyst to establish and strengthen relationships among those involved and helps to export the benefits to a wider societal context. A notable new example is the plan of Big Brothers/Big Sisters to ask all bigs and littles to work together in community projects, as part of being Big Brothers and Big Sisters. …

ai_analysis.title_ko: 세대 간 전략 촉진: 국가봉사단의 역할
ai_analysis.abstract_ko: 미국은 도전을 극복하기 위해 시민들의 관대함과 헌신에 의존해 왔습니다. 오늘날 수백만 명의 미국인이 자원봉사 활동에 참여하고 있으며, 정부의 규모가 축소됨에 따라 시민의 힘을 활용하는 것이 더욱 중요해지고 있습니다. 국가봉사단(Corporation for National Service)은 비영리 파트너들과 협력하여 자원봉사 부문을 강화하고 시민의 힘을 이끌어내고 있습니다. 55세 이상의 6천만 명에 달하는 고령층은 근로자, 부모, 조부모, 시민으로서 평생 쌓아온 기술과 경험이라는 독보적인 자산을 가지고 있습니다. 시니어봉사단, 아메리코프 등 국가봉사단의 프로그램은 세대 간 접근법이 확장되고 번영할 수 있는 광범위한 구조를 형성합니다. 세대 간 활동의 핵심 원리인 호혜성은 전국적인 프로그램에서 강화되며, 노인들은 어린이들의 독서를 지도하고 병원 환자를 돌보며 청소년 부모와 수감자들을 돕는 등 다양한 세대 간 교류를 실천하고 있습니다.
summary_3lines: 정부의 역할이 축소되는 시대에 시민들의 자원봉사 역량과 특히 55세 이상 고령층의 경험을 활용하는 국가적 전략의 필요성을 강조함.
국가봉사단(Corporation for National Service)의 다양한 프로그램을 통해 세대 간 호혜적 교류와 지역사회 문제 해결 성과를 도출함.
국립공원 현장에서 자원봉사 프로그램 기획 시 고령층의 전문성과 세대 간 협력을 결합한 운영 방안을 시사함.
ai_analysis.research_purpose: 이 논문은 정부의 자원 축소 시대에 대응하여 시민의 자발적 에너지, 특히 55세 이상 고령층의 평생 경험과 기술을 활용하기 위한 국가봉사단의 역할과 세대 간 협력 프로그램의 운영 구조를 분석하는 것을 목적으로 합니다.
key_findings: 55세 이상의 고령층은 타 연령대가 가지지 못한 평생의 기술과 경험을 보유한 강력한 자원봉사 자원임.
국가봉사단의 프로그램은 세대 간 호혜성을 바탕으로 청소년과 노인 간의 상호 보완적 교류를 촉진함.
시민사회와 비영리 파트너십을 통한 자원봉사 동원은 교육, 환경, 공공안전 등 다양한 사회적 수요를 효과적으로 충족시킴.
practical_applications: 국립공원 자원봉사자 모집 시 55세 이상 은퇴 전문가 및 시니어 세대의 경력을 활용할 수 있는 맞춤형 탐방 해설 및 환경 정화 직무를 신설한다.
고령의 자원봉사자와 청소년 및 지역 아동이 함께 참여하는 세대 간 생태 교육 및 탐방 안내 프로그램을 기획·운영한다.
지역사회 비영리단체 및 주민들과의 협력 거버넌스를 구축하여 공원 관리 및 자원 보호 활동에 시민 참여를 활성화한다.
ai_analysis.korea_np_applicability_reason: 한국 국립공원도 자원봉사자 및 시니어 레인저 제도를 운영하고 있어 고령층의 경력을 활용한 탐방 해설 및 공원 관리 프로그램에 직접 적용할 수 있으나, 미국의 국가봉사단과 같은 거대 조직 체계와는 제도적 차이가 있음.
field_checklist: 공원 내 시니어 및 세대 간 협력 자원봉사 프로그램 운영 현황을 확인한다.
참여 자원봉사자의 연령대별 보유 기술과 경력 데이터를 구축했는지 점검한다.
청소년과 고령층이 함께 참여할 수 있는 호혜적 프로그램이 마련되어 있는지 확인한다.
자원봉사자 교육 및 안전수칙 준수 여부를 정기적으로 모니터링한다.
지역사회 비영리단체와의 협력 체계가 원활히 작동하는지 평가한다.
cautions: 고령 자원봉사자 활동 시 야외 현장 활동에 따른 안전사고 예방 대책을 철저히 수립해야 한다.
국내 법령 및 공단 지침에 부합하는 자원봉사자 운영 규정과 예산 지원 방안을 사전에 검토해야 한다.
recommended_followup_research: 국립공원 내 고령층 자원봉사자의 참여 동기와 만족도가 공원 관리 기여도에 미치는 영향 분석

papers.title: Sonoran Desert Conservation
papers.abstract: The Sonoran Desert comes alive with colors in March. In wet years like this one, yellow and orange Mexican poppies, blue lupines, white chicories, pink parry penstemons, and tiny lavender sand bells carpet the land in a floral display that surpasses the imagination. Creosote and brittle bushes display yellow flowers while a few early-blooming chollas and hedgehog cacti show off their large, bright red ones. Tall, sharply spined saguaros and rounded barrel cacti stand guard over the desert, and cactus-like ocotillos sport dainty red flowers at the tips of long, thin branches that sway in the wind. “This is some of the best habitat in the whole desert,” states Gene Dahlem, a Bureau of Land Management (BLM) resource advisor. Dahlem speaks as he drives through the Sonoran Desert National Monument, one of 19 new national monuments created by President Bill Clinton and Interior Secretary Bruce Babbitt during their last year in office. Located halfway between Tucson and Phoenix, the national monument protects 486,000 acres of low mountains, desert thorn scrub, and creosote flats. It includes three congressionally designated national wilderness areas and the remnants of a small, long-abandoned copper mine. Creation of the Sonoran Desert National Monument is part of a much bigger effort to protect large sections of the desert and adjacent lands from further development. Growing populations in Tucson, Phoenix, and other cities threaten the desert with urban sprawl, while energy development could crisscross even the most remote areas with transmission lines. In all, two new national monuments and a new national conservation area have been designated in the Tucson area, and other new or expanded national, state, and county parks have been proposed. Together, the effort to protect the Sonoran Desert represents one of the most ambitious, ecosystem-wide conservation efforts currently under way in the United States. The Sonoran Desert encompasses 120,000 square miles of southern and western Arizona, southeastern California, the Mexican state of Sonora, and most of the Baja Peninsula. In Arizona, the desert runs from west of Nogales on the US–Mexican border north to east of Tucson and Phoenix, and then northwest to near Kingman. It is one of four North American deserts. The Chihuahuan Desert covers southwestern Texas, southern New Mexico, a bit of southeastern Arizona, and northeastern Mexico. The Great Basin Desert stretches from western Colorado across most of Utah and Nevada and into southwestern Idaho, southeastern Oregon, and eastern California. The Mojave Desert, the smallest of the four, includes southern Nevada, northwestern Arizona, and eastern California. By comparison with most deserts, the Sonoran is quite lush. Winter and summer rains over much of its area support a rich growth of saguaro, organ pipe, barrel, cholla, and prickly pear cacti; bushes like creosote and ocotillo; and numerous agaves and yuccas. The desert is also characterized by palo verdes, mesquites, ironwoods, and acacias, legume trees that grow in the low valleys and hillsides, especially along washes. Tall mountains near the desert's eastern margins are covered with thick forests of junipers, oaks, pines, and spruces, trees usually found much farther north. All told, the Sonoran Desert has more than 2,000 plant species—300 of which are cacti—and more than 550 vertebrate species. Even before new preserves were created or proposed, national, state, and county parks protected large swaths of the Sonoran Desert and adjacent lands in Arizona. The largest is Cabeza Prieta National Wildlife Refuge, which covers 860,000 acres of desert thorn scrub west of Ajo. Further south along the US– Mexican border, Organ Pipe Cactus National Monument protects 330,000 acres. South of Tucson, Buenos Aires National Wildlife Refuge features 116,000 acres of semiarid grasslands, marshes, and woodlands. Closer to Tucson, Saguaro National Park is divided into two sections that total some 93,000 acres of saguaro and palo verde forests. Coronado National Forest includes most of the Santa Catalina Mountains to Tucson's north, the Rincons to the east, and the Santa Ritas to the south. Two state parks north of Tucson—Catalina along the western slopes of the Santa Catalina Mountains and Picacho Peak—add nearly 9,000 acres. And Pima County's Tucson and Tortolita Mountain Parks, plus Colossal Cave Park, protect another 28,000 acres. The combination of exotic natural areas, year-round warm weather, and little rain has helped fuel an influx of people into Arizona that has increased the state's population by 40 percent since 1990. Tucson alone has grown from a mere 250 people in 1865 to 486,000 in 2000, up 20 percent in just the last decade. Pima County, which includes Tucson and most of south-central Arizona, now numbers nearly 850,000, a 26-percent increase since 1990. New construction to accommodate a growing Tucson consumes an estimated 6,400 acres of Sonoran Desert a year. It was in Tucson's northwest suburbs in 1997 that sprawl met the cactus ferruginous pygmy owl, an endangered subspecies. At two and one-half ounces, the cactus ferruginous pygmy owl is one of the smallest and least common of owls. The owl was once found in wooded riparian areas of the Sonoran Desert from the Gulf of California to central Arizona. It is also found in Texas and northeastern Mexico along the Gulf Coast. The owl's range in Arizona has dwindled as rivers, creeks, and washes dried up because of groundwater pumping and expansion of the built-up city. Only a dozen birds were known to reside in the Tucson area in 1977. More recent surveys have found about 70 owls and 13 active nests, most around Tucson and Organ Pipe Cactus National Monument, says Scott Richardson, an Arizona Game and Fish Department urban wildlife specialist. The discovery of cactus ferruginous pygmy owls forced the county to shelve plans for a school, mall, and other buildings that were to be part of a new development northwest of Tucson. It also sparked a renewed interest in conserving the Sonoran Desert and adjacent lands to protect the owl and other species. And it helped to launch a series of surveys that would extend our knowledge of the owl and other species and form the basis for a major conservation planning effort. “The owl has been the impetus for everything we're doing here,” says Carolyn Campbell, executive director of the Coalition for Sonoran Desert Protection, a Tucson-based environmental group. “We had not previously had to deal with an endangered species or to address issues of development,” adds Maeveen Behan about the problems raised by the cactus ferruginous pygmy owl. Pima County faced the prospect of lawsuits and having to seek incidental take permits from the US Fish and Wildlife Service (FWS) for every new development. “We realized that the only way to get out [from the requirements of the Endangered Species Act] was to commit to protecting the species,” says Behan, an assistant to the county administrator who heads the planning effort to conserve the Sonoran Desert. That realization led to Pima County's first attempt to regulate growth in the Sonoran Desert for environmental purposes. Behan and her boss began a series of meetings in 1998 with land-use planners, environmentalists, developers, ranchers, and others that led the county board of supervisors to undertake development of a multispecies habitat conservation plan. “We decided not just to mitigate or slow the decline of the owl, but to place biology in front of development,” she says. “Our goal was the owl's recovery.” The process involved the creation of various committees, task forces, and advisory teams; the hiring of contractors to conduct studies and write reports; and the holding of dozens of public meetings across the county. Babbitt, a former Arizona governor, declared the pygmy owl one of his top priorities, while Rep. Jim Kolbe (R-Ariz.) lobbied Congress to appropriate $3 million to fund the planning process. The county has issued more than 100 reports over the past three years, which, stacked one atop another, make a pile more than 3 feet tall. Individual reports deal with priority conservation areas, riparian recovery, vulnerable species, cultural and historic preservation, mountain parks, and ranch conservation. Key to the whole effort, says William Shaw, chairman of the scientific advisory team, was to ensure the scientific credibility of the planning process. He and his eight-member advisory team helped pull relevant information together, generated lists of species to study, identified experts to examine data and write reports, and reviewed their work. “If we did a good job, we will have helped preserve all species in Pima County,” adds Shaw, professor and chairman of the University of Arizona's wildlife and fisheries sciences department. “We want to incorporate science and conservation into local land-use planning.” For starters, the scientists identified 56 plants and animals that were endangered, threatened, or vulnerable in Pima County even if they were still plentiful elsewhere. The list featured the cactus ferruginous pygmy owl as well as the burrowing owl, southwestern willow flycatcher, Swainson's hawk, Merriam's mouse, Arizona shrew, the lowland and Chiricahua leopard frogs, desert pupfish, and seven species of bats. Plants included the pima pineapple, Nichol's Turk's head, and acuna, all barrel-like cacti. Even a pseudoscorpion was included. Next, the county hired experts who identified areas where each of the 56 vulnerable species were found or where suitable habitat existed. The experts generated a series of maps that delineated areas of no, low, medium, and high potential habitat for each. When laid one on top of each other, the maps yielded 2.1 million acres of land in Pima County where preservation would aid one or more of the species. The scientists further divided the area into core zones where biodiversity conservation should be the primary focus, other areas that would be of value for conservation, and still others that could serve as links or corridors to other protected areas or to areas that could be restored to provide habitat. The 2.1 million acres would not be one large park or refuge, Shaw says. Rather, the county's proposed plan will present alternative conservation strategies for local officials and the public to consider. Each strategy sets out different amounts of land to be protected and requirements that developers and others who want to use the land will have to meet. Following another series of public meetings, an 80-member steering committee will make recommendations to the county board. Behan hopes county officials can select a preferred alternative and adopt a funding scheme for the multi species habitat conservation plan by next summer, with FWS approval by the end of 2002. Whatever alternative is adopted, Behan and Shaw say, new and expanded parks and preserves are likely. Although which existing parks and how much land would be preserved is still unknown, some possibilities have already been identified. One is Tortolita Mountain Park, a county park north of Tucson, which could grow from its current 3,400 acres to 37,700. Two others are Colossal Cave, which could jump from 2,500 acres to 21,000, and Cienega Creek Natural Preserve, southeast of Tucson, which might increase from 4,000 to 36,000 acres. Similarly, several new parks might be created. These include a 10,700-acre park in the foothills of the Santa Rita Mountains southeast of Tucson and a 12,000-acre conservation area in the Cerro Colorado Mountains southwest of the city. Both would protect existing ranches. New tax incentives would also be adopted to help keep the 1.4-million acres of privately owned ranches in Pima County—which are largely open space—operating as ranches rather than being sold for development. To date, most Tucsonians seem to support the plan. “We can't continue to grow willy-nilly without creating problems,” says Mac Donaldson, a partner in the 72,000-acre Empire-Cienega Ranch southeast of Tucson. “We can make the plan work for ranchers. If we fight it, we'll lose because the population centers outnumber us. We can use the plan to continue our ability to ranch and to have our children and grandchildren ranch.” But not all agree. “We don't know what the cost will be or what opportunities we will lose,” says Alan Lurie, executive vice president of the Southern Arizona Home Builders Association, of the proposals to create new parks and put restrictions on development. Lurie cites recently adopted Pima County ordinances that require developers to leave natural 80 percent of land they build on in sensitive areas. “That's pretty far-reaching,” Lurie says, adding that he and other developers still hope the conservation planning process “will be good for all players.” Meanwhile, early in the planning process, scientists from the Arizona– Sonora Desert Museum in Tucson recommended that the county protect an area of Sonoran Desert in the Silverbell, Waterman, and Sawtooth Mountains northwest of the city. The area, known for its plentiful ironwood trees, contains very good habitat for cactus ferruginous pygmy owls, says Tony Herrell, a field manager for the Bureau of Land Management. Ironwoods are slow-growing, long-lived trees with extremely hard wood. At up to 35 feet, they are easily the tallest trees in the desert. Ironwoods provide shade and protection for young saguaros and other desert plants. Their presence can increase the number of bird species in an area by nearly two-thirds. Instead of creating a county park, though, local officials asked the federal government to act instead. Babbitt agreed and, after several public meetings, Clinton created the 129,000-acre Ironwood Forest National Monument in June 2000. Before the land can be fully protected, however, BLM officials will have to address several issues. One involves the 650 miles of unpaved roads that crisscross the monument. Used by local residents and hunters, the roads provide access to people who illegally dump trash, engage in target shooting, and hold high school drinking parties. Other issues include grazing rights within the monument and natural gas pipelines and electricity transmission lines through it. “We have to decide whether to continue those,” Herrell says. A thornier issue involves 56,000 acres of state trust lands now surrounded by the national monument. Trust lands were deeded to Arizona when it became a state to generate money for education and other public programs. Most state trust lands are leased for cattle grazing and mining, but others have been sold for development. Arizona objected to the creation of the national monument because it would limit the state's ability to generate income from the lands. So far, Arizona has declined to commit or sell any of its state trust lands for Sonoran Desert conservation. More immediately (in March), Gail Norton, President George W. Bush's new interior secretary, asked more than 400 congressional, state, local, and tribal leaders from areas around the 19 new national monuments how those places should be protected and used. In reply, a copper mining company suggested that a 900-acre section be withdrawn from Ironwood Forest National Monument. Although the company offered a 400-acre site in return, the 900-acre site includes areas used by the last bighorn sheep herd near Tucson. Elsewhere, following five years of planning, debate, and public meetings, Congress created the 42,000-acre Las Cienegas (Spanish for “wetland”) National Conservation Area southeast of Tucson in 2000. The conservation area lies in the Sonoita Plains, an arid grassland in southeastern Arizona that acts as a transition zone between the Sonoran Desert to the west and the Chihuahuan Desert to the east. It features a pronghorn herd that numbers about 100 and Cienega Creek, a north-flowing stream that, unlike most desert waterways, has water year round. Cattails, rushes, and sedges grow in the creek's shallows while cottonwoods and willows line the banks. As with the new national monuments, the law creating Las Cienegas restricts new mining claims, limits vehicles to designated roads, forbids new development, and directs BLM to conserve and protect its natural and cultural resources. The agency has laid out alternate conservation strategies for managing existing cattle grazing, restoring native species such as the endangered Gila topminnow, and enabling hiking and other public uses.
