papers.title: Pastoralism and Resulting Challenges for National Parks in Afar, Ethiopia
papers.abstract: Pastoralists and national parks are key stakeholders in the management and conservation of natural and protected habitats. In Ethiopia, Afar pastoralists migrate seasonally with their livestock in search for grazing and water areas. Livestock are also a source of infectious diseases that can spread into wildlife populations when pastoralists encroach into unfenced national parks. The interactions between pastoralists and national parks, as well as the subsequent impacts, remain insufficiently understood in Afar. Two structured questionnaire surveys were conducted in 2021, including 300 pastoralist households in seven woredas of Afar, and 58 staff from three national parks (Awash, Alidegi and Yangudi Rassa). They captured pastoralist movements and livestock diseases as well as the perception of national park staff regarding challenges resulting from pastoral encroachment into parks. Among the pastoralists, 74.7% migrated with their livestock for a mean 3.5 months per year, during which time, 90% of respondents reported contact with other livestock herds, and over 80% with wildlife. A third (34.2%) reported disease outbreaks in their village prior to migration. Pastoralists traveled long distances, crossing woreda, regional or national boundaries. All 58-park respondents reported pastoralists with livestock inside their park and their close contact with wildlife. Additionally, 69% reported the presence of domestic dogs. Wildlife displacement, habitat loss and dog attacks on wildlife were perceived as the main threat caused by the presence of pastoralists, whereas diseases were only mentioned by 15.5%. Overall, park staff showed poor disease knowledge. They reported poor disease surveillance and no disease response. Within pastoral contexts, improved collaboration between wildlife and livestock authorities regarding land use, disease awareness and surveillance is needed to balance the needs of both wildlife and pastoralist's livestock development and mitigate threats to wildlife habitats.

ai_analysis.title_ko: 에티오피아 아파르 지역의 유목민 활동과 국립공원이 직면한 과제
ai_analysis.abstract_ko: 유목민과 국립공원은 자연 및 보호지역 관리와 보전에 있어 핵심 이해관계자입니다. 에티오피아 아파르 지역의 유목민들은 방목지와 수자원을 찾아 가축과 함께 계절별로 이동합니다. 울타리가 없는 국립공원으로 유목민들이 침입할 때 가축은 야생동물 집단으로 전파될 수 있는 감염병의 매개체가 되기도 합니다. 아파르 지역에서는 유목민과 국립공원 간의 상호작용 및 그로 인한 영향에 대해 아직 충분히 이해되지 않고 있습니다. 2021년에 아파르 지역 7개 행정구역(woredas)의 300개 유목민 가구와 3개 국립공원(아와시, 알리데기, 양구디 라사)의 직원 58명을 대상으로 두 건의 구조화된 설문조사가 실시되었습니다. 이 조사는 유목민의 이동 경로, 가축 질병, 그리고 공원 내 유목민 침입으로 인한 과제에 대한 공원 직원의 인식을 파악했습니다. 조사 결과, 유목민의 74.7%가 가축과 함께 연평균 3.5개월 동안 이동했으며, 이 기간 동안 응답자의 90%는 다른 가축 떼와, 80% 이상은 야생동물과 접촉했다고 보고했습니다. 응답자의 3분의 1(34.2%)은 이동 전에 마을에서 질병 발생을 보고했습니다. 유목민들은 행정구역, 지역 또는 국가 경계를 넘나들며 장거리를 이동했습니다. 공원 직원 58명 전원은 공원 내에 가축을 동반한 유목민이 있으며 이들이 야생동물과 긴밀히 접촉하고 있다고 보고했습니다. 또한 69%는 반려견(가축견)의 존재를 보고했습니다. 유목민의 존재로 인해 야생동물 구축, 서식지 손실, 그리고 개에 의한 야생동물 공격이 주요 위협으로 인식된 반면, 질병은 15.5%만 언급되었습니다. 전반적으로 공원 직원의 질병 관련 지식은 부족했으며, 질병 감시 체계가 부실하고 대응 조치가 없는 것으로 나타났습니다. 유목민 맥락 내에서 야생동물과 가축 당국 간의 토지 이용, 질병 인식 및 감시에 대한 협력을 개선하여 야생동물과 유목민 가축의 요구를 조화시키고 야생동물 서식지에 대한 위협을 완화해야 합니다.
summary_3lines: 보호지역 내 유목민의 계절별 이동과 가축 방목이 야생동물 서식지에 미치는 영향과 관리 과제를 분석했습니다.
설문조사 결과, 유목민과 가축이 공원 내 야생동물과 광범위하게 접촉하며 서식지 훼손과 질병 전파 위험을 야기하고 있음을 확인했습니다.
효과적인 공원 관리를 위해 가축-야생동물 당국 간 협력 체계 구축 및 질병 모니터링 강화가 필요합니다.
ai_analysis.research_purpose: 본 연구는 에티오피아 아파르 지역의 국립공원과 인근 유목민 간의 상호작용 실태를 파악하고, 유목민의 가축 방목 및 이동이 야생동물 서식지와 질병 전파에 미치는 영향을 분석하는 것을 목적으로 합니다. 특히 공원 직원의 인식 조사를 통해 보호지역 관리의 취약점을 진단하고자 하였습니다.
key_findings: 유목민의 74.7%가 연평균 3.5개월 동안 가축과 함께 이동하며, 이 과정에서 80% 이상이 야생동물과 접촉함
공원 직원 전원이 공원 내 가축 방목과 야생동물 간의 근접 접촉을 확인했으며, 69%는 동반된 개(반려견)로 인한 위협을 보고함
공원 직원들의 질병 관련 전문 지식과 현장 모니터링 및 대응 체계가 매우 부족한 것으로 나타남
practical_applications: 가축 방목이 빈번한 공원 경계부 및 내부 지역에 대한 야생동물-가축 간 접촉 실태 정밀 조사 실시
보호지역 내 유입되는 반려견 및 가축 관리 강화를 위한 지역사회 연계 계도 활동 전개
가축 전염병의 야생동물 전파 차단을 위해 방역·축산 부서와 합동 질병 감시 체계 구축
ai_analysis.korea_np_applicability_reason: 한국 국립공원은 유목 문화가 없고 엄격한 공원구역 및 사유지 관리 제도가 정착되어 있어 본문의 유목민 침입 사례와 직접 일치하지는 않습니다. 다만, 인근 농·축가에서 유입되는 방목 가축, 유기견의 야생동물 위협, 그리고 부처 간 협업 부족 문제는 일부 유사하게 적용될 수 있습니다.
related_laws: 야생생물 보호 및 관리에 관한 법률 제8조
field_checklist: 공원 내외부 불법 방목 가축 및 유기견 출몰 빈도 확인
야생동물 서식지 내 가축 배설물 및 질병 매개 흔적 조사
인근 축산 농가와의 가축 질병 정보 공유 체계 유무 확인
공원 관리 인력의 야생동물 질병 관련 교육 이수 여부 점검
지역 주민 및 축산 농가 대상 완충지역 내 행위 제한 홍보 실태 점검
cautions: 에티오피아의 전통적 유목 문화와 한국의 정주형 농축산 환경은 차이가 있으므로 제도를 그대로 원용하기는 부적절합니다.
가축 질병 및 방역 문제는 공원관리청 단독 권한이 아니므로 지자체 및 농림축산부서와의 공식적인 협조 체계가 전제되어야 합니다.
recommended_followup_research: 보호지역 인근 가축 방목이 멸종위기 야생생물의 행동권 및 스트레스에 미치는 영향 분석
국립공원 경계부 유기견 및 방목 가축으로 인한 인수공통전염병 전파 실태 조사

papers.title: Preliminary strong ground motion simulation at seismic stations within nuclear power plant sites in South Korea by a scenario earthquake on the causative fault of 2016 Gyeongju earthquake
papers.abstract: Stochastic and an empirical Green's function (EGF) methods are preliminarily applied to simulate strong ground motions (SGMs) at seismic stations within nuclear power plant (NPP) sites in South Korea by an assumed large earthquake with MW6.5 (scenario earthquake) on the causative fault of the 2016 Gyeongju earthquake with MW5.5 (mainshock). In the stochastic method, a ratio of spectral amplitudes of observed and simulated waveforms for the mainshock is assumed to be an adjustment factor. In the EGF method, SGMs by the mainshock are simulated assuming SGMs by the 2016 Gyeongju earthquake with MW5.0 (foreshock) as the EGF. To simulate SGMs by the scenario earthquake, a ratio of fault length to width is assumed to be 2:1 in the stochastic method, and SGMs by the mainshock are assumed to be EGF in the EGF method. The results are similar based on a bias of the simulated response spectra by the two methods, and the simulated response spectra by the two methods exceeded commonly standard design response spectra anchored at 0.3 g of NPP sites slightly at a frequency band above 4 Hz, but considerable attention to interpretation is required since it is an indirect comparison.

ai_analysis.title_ko: 2016년 경주 지진 유발斷層을 이용한 시나리오 지진 기반 국내 원전 부지 내 지진관측소 강진동 예비 모의
ai_analysis.abstract_ko: 본 연구에서는 2016년 규모 5.5의 경주 지진을 유발한 단층에서 규모 6.5의 가상 대지진(시나리오 지진)이 발생했을 때, 한국 내 원전 부지 내 지진관측소에서의 강진동을 모의하기 위해 확률론적 방법과 경험적 그린함수(EGF) 방법을 예비 적용하였다. 확률론적 방법에서는 본진의 관측 파형과 모의 파형의 스펙트럼 진폭비를 보정 계수로 가정하였고, EGF 방법에서는 2016년 규모 5.0의 전진을 EGF로 가정하여 본진의 강진동을 모의하였다. 시나리오 지진에 의한 강진동을 모의하기 위해 확률론적 방법에서는 단층의 길이 대 폭 비율을 2:1로 가정하였으며, EGF 방법에서는 본진에 의한 강진동을 EGF로 가정하였다. 두 가지 방법에 의해 모의된 응답 스펙트럼의 편차를 바탕으로 한 결과는 유사하였으며, 두 방법에 의해 모의된 응답 스펙트럼은 4 Hz 이상의 주파수 대역에서 원전 부지의 0.3 g 기준 설계응답스펙트럼을 약간 상회하였다. 다만 이는 간접적인 비교이므로 해석 시 상당한 주의가 요구된다.
summary_3lines: 2016년 경주 지진 단층을 활용한 가상 대지진 시나리오 기반의 원전 부지 강진동 모의를 수행하였다.
확률론적 방법과 경험적 그린함수(EGF) 방법을 적용하여 지진동을 모의한 결과, 고주파수 영역에서 기존 설계기준을 약간 상회하는 응답 스펙트럼이 나타났다.
본 연구 결과는 지진 재해 대비 시설물 안전성 평가 및 지진동 모의 방법론 검토를 위한 기초 자료로 활용될 수 있다.
ai_analysis.research_purpose: 2016년 경주 지진의 단층을 기준으로 규모 6.5의 가상 대지진 발생 시 국내 원전 부지 내 지진관측소에 미칠 강진동을 예측하고, 확률론적 방법과 경험적 그린함수(EGF) 방법의 적용성을 비교 검토하기 위함이다.
key_findings: 확률론적 방법과 경험적 그린함수(EGF) 방법을 이용한 강진동 모의 결과가 상호 유사한 경향을 보였다.
두 방법 모두 4 Hz 이상의 고주파수 대역에서 원전 부지의 표준 설계응답스펙트럼(0.3 g 기준)을 약간 상회하였다.
가상 대지진 시나리오 적용 시 단층 기하학적 특성과 전·본진 관계를 고려한 강진동 예측의 유효성을 확인하였다.
practical_applications: 국립공원 내 주요 탐방 기반시설 및 방재 시설물의 내진 성능 기준 검토 시 지진동 모의 방법론 참고
지진 발생 시나리오에 따른 공원 내 지진관측소 및 재난 모니터링 시스템의 대응력 점검
고주파수 대역 지진파가 국립공원 내 노후 시설물에 미치는 영향 분석 및 보강 대책 수립
ai_analysis.korea_np_applicability_reason: 원전 부지를 대상으로 한 지진동 모의 연구로 국립공원 생태계나 탐방로 관리와는 직접적인 관련이 적으나, 공원 내 재난 안전 관리 및 시설물 내진 설계 분야에 간접적으로 시사점을 제공한다.
field_checklist: 공원 내 지진관측소 및 방재 시설물의 위치와 작동 상태 확인
지진 발생 시 탐방객 대피소 및 주요 시설물의 내진 보강 여부 점검
과거 지진(예: 경주 지진 등) 발생 시 공원 내 시설물 피해 이력 조사
고주파수 지진동에 취약한 석조문화재 및 노후 탐방시설 점검
지진 재난 대응 매뉴얼 상의 현장 조치 행동요령 숙지
cautions: 본 연구는 원전 부지를 특정하여 수행된 시나리오 분석이므로 일반 국립공원 시설에 일률적 적용 시 한계가 있음
간접 비교에 기반한 결과이므로 현장 적용 시 지반 특성에 따른 세밀한 보정이 필요함
recommended_followup_research: 국립공원 주요 지반 특성을 반영한 부지 증폭 특성 연구
지진 시나리오에 따른 국립공원 탐방로 및 시설물 피해 위험도 평가 연구

papers.title: Cambrian series 3 agnostoid trilobitesPtychagnostus sinicusandPtychagnostus atavusfrom the Machari Formation, Yeongwol Group, Taebaeksan Basin, Korea
papers.abstract: Abstract This paper reports the successive occurrence of Ptychagnostus sinicus Lu, 1957 and Ptychagnostus atavus (Tullberg, 1880) from the lower part of the Machari Formation, Yeongwol Group, Korea. Morphometric approaches of using the landmark and principal component analyses make it possible to differentiate P . sinicus from P . atavus with clarity: pygidia of P . sinicus have a relatively narrow M1, a transverse F2, and a weakly developed M2 tubercle, whereas those of P . atavus are characterized by a broadly arching M1, a chevron-shaped F2, and a prominent M2 tubercle. Recognition of P . atavus , for the first time in Korea, allows the determination of the base of the Drumian Stage in Korea and aids correlation with other parts of the world.

ai_analysis.title_ko: 한국 태백산분지 영월그룹 마차리층에서 산출되는 캄브리아기 제3세 아그노스이드 삼엽충 프티카그노스투스 시니쿠스(Ptychagnostus sinicus)와 프티카그노스투스 아타부스(Ptychagnostus atavus)
ai_analysis.abstract_ko: 본 논문은 한국 영월그룹 마차리층 하부에서 프티카그노스투스 시니쿠스(Ptychagnostus sinicus Lu, 1957)와 프티카그노스투스 아타부스(Ptychagnostus atavus (Tullberg, 1880))의 연속적인 산출을 보고한다. 랜드마크 형태학적 기법과 주성분 분석을 활용한 형태측정 접근법을 통해 두 종을 명확하게 구분할 수 있었다. P. sinicus의 미부(꼬리마디)는 상대적으로 좁은 M1, 가로 방향의 F2, 그리고 약하게 발달한 M2 결절을 가지는 반면, P. 아타부스는 넓게 아치형을 이루는 M1, 쉐브론 형태의 F2, 그리고 돌출된 M2 결절을 특징으로 한다. 한국에서 최초로 P. 아타부스가 확인됨으로써 국내 드루미안절(Drumian Stage)의 하부 경계를 결정할 수 있게 되었으며, 전 세계 다른 지역과의 층서적 대비에 기여한다.
summary_3lines: 한국 영월그룹 마차리층에서 발견된 캄브리아기 삼엽충 화석의 형태학적 분석을 통해 지질학적 층서 기준을 확립하고자 하였다.
형태측정 분석 기법을 적용하여 유사한 두 삼엽충 종의 미부 형태적 차이를 명확히 규명하고 국내 최초로 특정 지질시대를 확인하였다.
이번 연구 결과는 국내 고생물 자원의 정밀한 층서학적 위치를 파악하고 지질유산의 학술적 가치를 높이는 데 활용될 수 있다.
ai_analysis.research_purpose: 본 연구는 태백산분지 영월그룹 마차리층 하부에서 채집된 아그노스이드 삼엽충 화석들의 형태적 특징을 정밀 분석하여 종을 구분하고, 이를 바탕으로 국내 지질 층서의 기준을 국제 표준과 대비하고자 수행되었다. 특히 기존에 구분이 모호했던 종들을 랜드마크 형태측정 분석과 주성분 분석을 통해 객관적으로 식별하고자 했다.
key_findings: Ptychagnostus sinicus와 Ptychagnostus atavus 두 삼엽충 종의 형태학적 차이를 미부(M1, F2, M2 결절 등)의 특징을 통해 명확하게 구분함.
한국 내에서 Ptychagnostus atavus의 존재를 최초로 확인하여 국내 지질 층서학적 편년의 정확도를 높임.
화석의 층서적 출현을 바탕으로 국내 캄브리아기 드루미안절(Drumian Stage)의 하부 경계를 설정하고 세계 다른 지역과의 대비가 가능해짐.
practical_applications: 국립공원 내 고생물 화석 산출지의 정밀 지질 조사 및 학술적 가치 평가 시 형태측정 분석 기법 적용
지질공원(Geopark) 운영 시 공원 내 중요 지질유산의 연대 측정 및 층서 대비 자료로 활용
탐방객 대상 지질·화석 해설 프로그램 운영 시 정확한 고생물학적 학술 정보 제공
ai_analysis.korea_np_applicability_reason: 본 연구는 특정 지역의 학술적 고생물 화석 층서 연구로, 태백산권 등 지질공원이나 국립공원의 지자체 관리 지역 내 지질 자원 보전 및 학술 조사에는 일부 기여하나, 일반적인 현장 탐방객 관리나 생태계 관리 실무에 직접 적용하기에는 거리가 있음.
field_checklist: 공원 내 지질유산 및 화석 산출지 주변 훼손 여부 확인
학술조사 허가 지역 내 무단 채집 및 훼손 행위 모니터링
지질 명소 안내판의 고생물 연대 및 학명 정보 최신화 여부 점검
중요 지질 자원 보호를 위한 출입통제 시설 및 표지판 상태 확인
지질공원 해설사 대상 최신 고생물학 연구 성과 교육 실시 여부 확인
cautions: 화석 산출지는 문화재보호법 또는 자연공원법에 따라 엄격히 보호되므로 무단 채집이나 훼손에 주의해야 함.
본 연구는 고도의 전문적 형태측정 분석을 다루므로 현장 실무자가 직접 분석하기보다는 전문가 자문이 필요함.
recommended_followup_research: 태백산분지 내 다른 캄브리아기 지층에서의 추가 화석 발굴 및 층서 대비 연구
지질유산 보호를 위한 국립공원 내 고생물 산출지 정밀 실태조사

papers.title: The Haitian Earthquake and Academic Emergency Medicine
papers.abstract: “… everyone has a heart that is sensitive to the suffering of others.”—Mencius On January 12, 2010, at 16:53 local time, a 7.0 Mw earthquake struck 25 km west of Port-au-Prince, Haiti, causing one of the worst disasters in human history. The world community responded with one of its greatest outpourings of concern and support. This article summarizes the response to that disaster, especially as it relates to emergency care, and describes the role of academic emergency medicine. We do not intend a rigorous academic analysis; Haiti was in many ways unique. Haiti is the poorest country in the Western Hemisphere, with a per-capita gross domestic product (GDP) of only 1,300 USD.1 This is corrected for local purchasing power (PPP), which means that it overestimates the ability of Haitians to purchase goods and services on the world market. Indeed, one of the immediate effects of the earthquake was to dramatically increase the local price of goods. According to our Haitian colleagues the price of food tripled in the first few days, and although food aid arrived quickly, the market price remains high. In addition, Haiti has little economic infrastructure, and perhaps one-fourth of its GDP is from remittances from Haitians working abroad. Haiti’s poverty is not only financial; it extends to basic natural and human resources. One of the most stunning examples of this is apparent when flying into the country. The east side of Hispaniola is within the Dominican Republic and much is verdant green. The west side of the island is Haiti and is almost completely deforested. The standard measure of human development is the United Nations Human Development Index (UN-HDI). This combines life expectancy, literacy, and school enrollment with the natural log of the per-capita GDP corrected for PPP. Haiti’s HDI is 0.532, which ranks it 149th of 182 countries. In addition, Haitian incomes are highly maldistributed and there are large income disparities. This is commonly measured with the Gini index, which compares a nation’s actual income distribution (the “Lorenz curve”) to the line of absolute equality. Haiti’s index is 59.2—the eighth worst among the 134 listed in the CIA’s Factbook.1 When the earthquake hit the initial damage was enormous. Estimates are that a quarter of a million people died, a third of a million were seriously injured, and over a million became homeless. All these numbers are probably crude estimates, because records were lost or never kept. When we drove through Port-au-Prince, most of the buildings appeared severely damaged or destroyed and few appeared safe. The survivors were living in tents made of bed sheets, pitched in open areas and parks throughout the city. By the second month after the quake, tens of thousands of multiperson tents had arrived and efforts were being made to provide waterproof tarps before the start of the rainy season. These may be the standard local housing for the next few years. Flying over the city in April, the city is dotted with blue tarps, marking the tent cities. The earthquake damaged or destroyed all of the local hospitals. Two days after the earthquake, only one hospital was in operation.2 Although many reopened quickly, unsafe buildings, demolished wards, and lost equipment meant that there was little surgical or inpatient care available. We were told that almost half of the physicians and nurses at the University Hospital were killed in the quake. The USNC Comfort and field hospitals provided most of the initial critical surgical capacity. The international response was quick and massive but was hampered by the destruction of the port and damage to the small international airport. Over 150 nations supplied support. Dozens if not hundreds of nongovernmental organizations (NGOs) were providing relief within days. Haiti has had a long dependency on outside aid, and perhaps 3000 NGOs were active before the quake.3 A total of 2.1 billion USD was donated in the first month, and an additional 1.3 billion USD was pledged. It is estimated that 11 billion are needed (http://www.reliefweb.int). For those of us with domestic experience in disaster medicine, this was a very atypical mission. The disaster was massive, orders of magnitude worse than the others we had responded to. The response was equally massive. Initially there was no clear overall disaster response framework. The UN Cluster system appeared to have failed, unlike the success seen in the Asian tsunami. There was little coordination among the initial players and no functioning referral systems. The lack of a clear and effective authority was a crux problem. The Haitian government was marginally effective prior to quake and heavily damaged. In fact, most government buildings were completely destroyed and many employees were killed. The direct effect of this was apparent when some of us delivered paperwork to government officials who had been forced to relocate to an upper-middle class residential area. This neighborhood appeared completely undamaged; even the stucco was intact. The UN had been responsible for peacekeeping and international coordination, but it also had been heavily damaged, and almost half of its staff and leadership were killed. As a result neither the Haitian government nor the UN was able to quickly transition to a disaster management team. This caused the vast number of NGOs and arriving aid workers to function in a highly uncoordinated environment, a situation that was described by early responders as a “free-for-all.” The situation was aggravated by the Haitian health care situation prior to the earthquake. Haiti is a low-resource setting with little marginal capacity. Although the demographic transition to an older urban population is well under way, “tropical” diseases are still common. Hepatitis A and B, malaria (chloroquine sensitive Plasmodium falciparum), dengue, typhoid, rabies, filariasis, leptospirosis, anthrax, tuberculosis, tetanus, and intestinal parasites are endemic. These infections are really diseases of poverty and most U.S. physicians are unfamiliar with their presentations. HIV/AIDS is declining (prevalence is estimated at only 2.3%), but it is most common in the urban young adults who make up the bulk of the Port-au-Prince population. In addition, responders faced persistent language barriers. Haiti is a Francophone- and Creole-speaking country in a hemisphere that speaks Spanish and English. Translation was difficult to arrange at first. We received reports that some NGOs had initially used members of international criminal gangs that had been freed when the national prison collapsed.4 The near-complete collapse of infrastructure made the usual model of disaster response untenable. In most disasters local resources, including established emergency services and spontaneous lay responders, provide the immediate life-saving response. However, this initial phase was hampered by baseline lack of resources and the scale of this disaster. Typically, this initial response is rapidly augmented by outside resources that respond to the disaster area and by the transfer of patients out of the disaster zone to undamaged facilities. The specifics of the earthquake and generally poor construction standards rendered the few remaining facilities unsafe. Consequently, few patients could be initially transferred. There was an immediate need for emergency care, particularly for trauma and orthopedic surgery, which overwhelmed both local resources and the initial response. What was needed was a very rapid response by self-contained medical units. Transportation, shelter, medical and surgical materials, supplies, sanitation equipment, security personnel, and even food and water needed to be externally supplied. Unsupported aid workers drained local resources and put themselves at risk. The necessary personal requirements were also unique. The ability to work in a chaotic environment was crucial. Workers needed to be flexible. They needed to be comfortable supplying surgical support and performing triage. Our patients included adults and children. Obstetric, neonatal, and mental health problems were common. The volume was huge and providers often needed to treat and discharge patients into the tent cities without being certain of the diagnosis. Physicians needed to be able to do their own tests and function with an extremely limited lab. A comprehensive knowledge base of “tropical” medicine, hygiene, and acute care was essential as were disaster response skills such as knowledge of communications, safety, and incident command. Emergency physicians and particularly academic emergency physicians seemed to be overrepresented among the early responders. We believe that this was because we have characteristics that make us uniquely suited for this role. Emergency physicians view disaster medicine as part of their field: multicasualty incidents are a regular occurrence, we train for hospital-based and regional disasters, formal education in disaster care is incorporated into residency programs, and emergency medicine offers fellowship training in disaster medicine. Disasters are, by definition, emergencies, and emergency physicians are used to working in chaos. Teamwork is essential in a disaster and emergency physicians are used to working in a flexible team environment. Academic physicians have specific advantages. The need for a very rapid response favors large physician groups with flexible time commitments. Disaster response is often viewed as a departmental mission; this means not only that providers are willing to go but that their colleagues are willing to back them up. In addition, we suspect that academics tend to have a broader knowledge base than most physicians, which is very useful when working in a foreign environment. This experience provided new lessons and the opportunity to reinforce lessons learned from prior disasters. While it may seem apparent, the balance between timeliness and the depth of the response is important. Small groups responded faster, but large teams brought infrastructure and breadth. Both were needed, and we have yet to achieve the correct balance. We also know that despite the scale, disasters are local events. As such, local knowledge was key, and working with local physicians was very helpful. Haitian physicians recognized illnesses and could determine, for example, that this febrile child probably did not have malaria because it was early in the season and it looked more like pneumonia. They were aware of local protocols and referral patterns. Their knowledge of local demographic and medical data reduced uncertainty and facilitated work-ups. Availability of a support structure was critical. Logistics, shelter, sanitation, and security are not done best by physicians. Pharmacy, radiology, and ultrasound were essential, as was operating capability. Emergency physicians are generally competent generalists, but we wish we were better at surgical assisting and obstetrics. Social issues were important; providers needed to understand the limitations of the scene and medical infrastructure. They needed to be willing to live and work in an austere environment and they needed to “check their ego at the border.” Would we do it again? Our patients and Haitian colleagues make that answer an easy yes. What is needed now is infrastructure. It will take years to rebuild shelter, water, and sanitation. Port-au-Prince needs better structures, building codes, and enforcement. A few tons of rebar would have made a huge difference. The social infrastructure also needs to be rebuilt. Educational facilities, in particular, were devastated. The disaster is not over, it is merely evolving. We believe that there is a long-term role for academic emergency medicine in helping to rebuild the medical infrastructure. Of course we will go back.

ai_analysis.title_ko: 아이티 대지진과 학술 응급의학
ai_analysis.abstract_ko: “모든 이의 마음에는 타인의 고통에 민감한 심장이 있다.” - 맹자. 2010년 1월 12일 현지 시각 오후 4시 53분, 아이티 포르토프랭스 서쪽 25km 지점에서 규모 7.0의 지진이 발생하여 인류 역사상 최악의 재난 중 하나를 야기했습니다. 국제사회는 이에 대해 지대한 관심과 지원을 보냈습니다. 이 논문은 해당 재난에 대한 대응, 특히 응급 의료와 관련된 부분을 요약하고 학술 응급의학의 역할을 기술합니다. 우리는 엄밀한 학술적 분석을 의도한 것은 아니며, 아이티의 상황은 여러 면에서 독특했습니다. 아이티는 서반구에서 가장 가난한 국가로 1인당 국내총생산(GDP)이 1,300달러에 불과합니다. 이는 구매력평가(PPP)를 반영한 것으로, 세계 시장에서 재화와 용역을 구매하는 아이티인들의 능력을 과대평가한 것입니다. 실제로 지진의 즉각적인 영향 중 하나는 현지 물가의 급격한 상승이었습니다. 아이티 동료들에 따르면 첫 며칠 동안 식품 가격이 세 배로 올랐으며, 식량 원조가 빠르게 도착했음에도 불구하고 시장 가격은 여전히 높습니다. 게다가 아이티는 경제 기반 시설이 거의 없고 GDP의 약 4분의 1이 해외 근로 송금액에 의존합니다. 아이티의 빈곤은 재정적 측면에만 국한되지 않으며 기초적인 자연 및 인적 자원까지 확장됩니다. 가장 놀라운 사례 중 하나는 입국할 때 비행기에서 확연히 드러납니다. 히스파니올라 섬의 동쪽은 도미니카 공화국으로 푸르른 녹음이 우거져 있지만, 섬의 서쪽인 아이티는 거의 완전히 벌거벗겨져 산림이 파괴되어 있습니다. 인간 발달의 표준 지표는 유엔인간개발지수(UN-HDI)입니다. 이는 기대수명, 문해력, 취학률과 PPP로 보정된 1인당 GDP의 자연로그를 결합한 것입니다. 아이티의 HDI는 0.532로 182개국 중 149위입니다. 또한 아이티의 소득 불평등은 매우 심각합니다. 이는 실제 소득 분배를 절대 평등선과 비교하는 지니계수로 흔히 측정됩니다. 아이티의 지수는 59.2로 CIA 팩트북에 등재된 134개국 중 8번째로 나쁩니다. 지진 발생 당시 초기 피해는 막대했습니다. 약 25만 명이 사망하고 33만 명이 중상을 입었으며 100만 명 이상이 노숙자가 된 것으로 추정됩니다. 기록이 유실되었거나 애초에 작성되지 않았기 때문에 이 모든 숫자는 아마도 대략적인 추정치에 불과합니다. 우리가 포르토프랭스를 차로 이동했을 때, 대부분의 건물은 심각하게 파손되거나 파괴되었고 안전해 보이는 곳은 거의 없었습니다. 생존자들은 도시 전역의 공터와 공원에 침대 시트로 만든 천막을 치고 살고 있었습니다. 지진 발생 두 달째가 되자 수만 개의 다인용 텐트가 도착했고 우기가 시작되기 전에 방수포를 제공하기 위한 노력이 이루어졌습니다. 이들은 향후 몇 년 동안 표준적인 현지 주거 형태가 될 수 있습니다. 4월에 도시 상공을 비행하며 바라본 도시의 모습은 참혹했습니다.
summary_3lines: 2010년 아이티 대지진 발생 당시의 응급 의료 대응 상황과 국제사회의 지원 실태를 조명함.
극심한 경제적 빈곤, 인프라 부재, 심각한 환경 훼손이 대형 재난 피해를 더욱 가중시켰음을 확인 함.
대형 재난 발생 시 현장의 물리적·경제적 한계를 고려한 신속하고 실효성 있는 응급 대응 체계 구축의 필요성을 시사함.
ai_analysis.research_purpose: 2010년 아이티 대지진 당시 발생한 인도주의적 위기와 응급 의료 대응 과정을 정리하고, 국가적 인프라와 경제적 수준이 재난 대응에 미치는 영향을 고찰하고자 함.
key_findings: 지진으로 인해 약 25만 명이 사망하고 100만 명 이상의 이재민이 발생하는 등 막대한 인명 및 재산 피해가 발생함.
아이티는 낮은 1인당 GDP와 극심한 소득 불평등, 취약한 경제 기반 시설로 인해 재난 대응 역량이 극도로 제한됨.
식품 가격 폭등 및 주거 시설 부족 등 2차 피해가 발생하였으며, 산림 벌채 등 심각한 환경 파괴가 재난 취약성을 높였음.
practical_applications: 국립공원 내 대규모 지진 등 재난 발생 시 신속한 임시 대피소 설치 및 응급 구호 물품 보급 매뉴얼을 정비함.
취약한 인프라 지역의 비상 통신망 및 의료 지원 체계를 사전에 점검하고 유관기관과의 협력 체계를 강화함.
재난 발생 초기 물가 상승 및 물류 마비 상황을 가정하여 탐방객 및 지역 주민 구호 대책을 수립함.
ai_analysis.korea_np_applicability_reason: 본 논문은 개발도상국의 극단적인 대규모 도시 지진과 국가적 재난 복구를 다루고 있어, 국내 국립공원의 자연재해 관리 체계와는 사회경제적 배경 및 현장 여건에서 차이가 큼.
field_checklist: 공원 내 대규모 자연재해 발생 시 비상 대피 장소 및 구호 물품 비축 현황을 확인했는가?
유관기관(소방, 경찰, 지자체)과의 긴급 응급 의료 및 구조 협력 체계가 구축되어 있는가?

papers.title: Perplexity and choice: challenges and future development of laver cultivation in Jiangsu Province, China
papers.abstract: Seaweed cultivation holds significant importance in addressing global challenges.On the one hand,it aids in alleviating the food crisis.On the other hand,it offers substantial ecological benefits,such as enhancing carbon sequestration,facilitating nitrogen cycling,and mitigating eutrophication(He et al.,2008;Wu et al.,2015;Mantri et al.,2023).Globally,the dominant cultivated economic seaweeds include Laminaria spp.,Kappaphycus spp.,Gracilaria spp.,Neopyropia spp.,and Undaria spp.(Park et al.,2021;Khan et al.,2024).In 2022,the annual global production of seaweed is estimated to be approximately 36.4 million metric tons(live weight),with red algae accounting for about 55.8% and brown algae for approximately 43.8%(FAO,2024).Asia constitutes the principal region for seaweed cultivation,representing over 97% of global production,with China(about 60%),Indonesia(about 25%),South Korea(about 5%),and the Philippines(about 4%)being the largest contributors to this industry(Khan et al.,2024;Liu et al.,2024).Among them,the Neopyropia species,a type of high-end red algae,is highly favored among consumers(Li et al.,2023)and possesses rich edible and medicinal values(Subramaniyan et al.,2021;Zhao et al.,2023).It is frequently utilized for the production of foods such as laver sushi and laver pancakes.Consequently,the significance of laver cultivation is self-evident.China boasts the world's largest laver cultivation area,with total production reaching 209,939 metric tons(dry weight)in 2023(Fishery Administration Bureau of Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs,2024).The main cultivated laver species include Neopyropia haitanensis,Neopyropia yezoensis,Neopyropia acanthophora,and Neopyropia dentata(Wang et al.,2020).Notably,Jiangsu Province,China,serves as the leading production area for the highly sought-after N.yezoensis(Figure 1).The N.yezoensis aquaculture industry in the Subei intertidal zone of Jiangsu Province originated in the 1970s of the 20th century(Liu et al.,2021a).After more than 50 years of development,the intertidal zone in Jiangsu Province has become the largest global N.yezoensis aquaculture area,leading both nationally and globally.For instance,in 2023,the area of laver cultivation in Jiangsu Province reached 33,393 hectares,approximately 51.81% of the total national laver cultivation area.During the same year,the production of laver in Jiangsu Province reached 35,936 metric tons(dry weight),accounting for about 17.12% of the total national laver production(Fishery Administration Bureau of Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs,2024).The industry is of considerable scale and has comprehensively enhanced the coastal economic development and industrial reputation of Jiangsu Province.Furthermore,many impoverished individuals have achieved poverty alleviation and wealth accumulation through seaweed cultivation(Li et al.,2011).Nevertheless,the laver cultivation industry in Jiangsu Province is progressively encountering certain challenges,such as extreme marine events and disasters.This opinion article aims to identify the key factors affecting laver cultivation in Jiangsu Province and proposes recommendations for its sustainable development.For the growth stages of seaweed,extreme climate changes can lead to cellular and subcellular damage in the thalli,ultimately affecting its growth,quality,and yield(Khan et al.,2024).Currently,the negative impact of climate change on seaweed aquaculture is a long-term and widespread issue encountered in global aquaculture processes(Veenhof et al.,2024),which is difficult to resolve effectively in the short term.Over the past six decades,the sea surface temperature in the Southern Yellow Sea(SYS)has generally shown an increasing trend,with a warming amplitude of approximately 0.61°C.This indicates that under the backdrop of global warming,the SYS region has exhibited a warming trend(Guo et al.,2024).Concurrently,the interannual and multidecadal variability of sea surface temperature in the SYS is also associated with large-scale climatic factors such as El Niño-Southern Oscillation(ENSO)and Pacific Decadal Oscillation(PDO)(Wang & Yu,2014),leading to anomalous warming of regional seawater temperatures in certain years.Elevated seawater temperatures indirectly promote the frequent occurrence of diseases and other factors that hinder the growth of N.yezoensis.Currently,climate warming is leading to frequent occurrences of seedling rot,slow growth,and significant reductions in yield during the cultivation of Neopyropia,resulting in economic losses for the laver cultivation industry in the SYS region in recent years(Figure 2A).For instance,from late 2016 to mid-2017,influenced by factors such as abnormally high temperatures in the Haizhou Bay area,the production of N.yezoensis in Lianyun District,Lianyungang City,Jiangsu Province,was severely reduced,with a decrease of about 60% compared to the previous year(Lianyun District People's Government,2017).Extreme weather events triggered by climate change also warrant attention.At the end of April 2021,an infrequent event featuring extreme winds and thunderstorms occurred in the Subei intertidal zone of the SYS,with wind gusts reaching level 14.This event resulted in direct economic losses exceeding 140 million RMB Yuan in Nantong City,Jiangsu Province(Lu & Du,2022),and the large-scale collapse of Neopyropia cultivation rafts(Lu & Du,2022).Tens of thousands of raft components,including ropes and bamboo poles(Figure 2B),are being swept into the ocean(Sun et al.,2022a),causing economic losses to laver farmers.It affected the smooth progress of the Neopyropia raft recovery operations,and in addition,caused casualties,either directly or indirectly(CCTV,2021).Similarly,in January 2016,Lianyungang City,Jiangsu Province experienced severe sea ice and strong winds caused by extremely cold weather.This affected over 7,000 hectares of N.yezoensis cultivation area,leading to incalculable economic losses for local farmers(Sohu,2016).In addition,rising global CO2 concentrations contribute to ocean acidification,which can impact interspecific competition among seaweeds(Feng et al.,2024).Although the elevated CO2 levels alleviate the competitive relationship between N.yezoensis and the harmful epiphyte Ulva species(e.g.,Ulva prolifera),the long-term perspective indicates a growing competitive advantage for Ulva under this climate change scenario(Sun et al.,2021).Traditionally,N.yezoensis is considered a cold-tolerant seaweed,whereas U.prolifera exhibits a greater capacity to endure higher temperatures compared to N.yezoensis.Micropropagules of U.prolifera are persistently present in the SYS region(Cao et al.,2023;Xia et al.,2024a),and the areas on the raft components not colonized by laver are also conducive to the attachment of U.prolifera,leading to the subsequent occupation of ecological niches by U.prolifera on the raft structures(Zhang et al.,2019a).Concurrently,as U.prolifera matures,it demonstrates a stronger ability to absorb nutrients than N.yezoensis,thereby allowing the epiphytically growing U.prolifera to gradually establish a growth advantage(Shan,2022).This results in Ulva species with an enhanced capability to occupy ecological niches,which subsequently impacts the normal growth of laver and affects the future development of Neopyropia aquaculture in the SYS region.Neopyropia yezoensis is susceptible to various diseases during cultivation and growth due to the impact of global climate change,harmful microbial infection,and overcrowding during cultivation(Kim et al.,2014).Common diseases include seedling rot,chytrid blight,green spot disease,and white rot(Qiu et al.,2019;Yang et al.,2020;Bae et al.,2024),which frequently lead to the genetic characterization decline of laver populations.In addition,the coastal waters of Jiangsu Province are severely eutrophic(Liu et al.,2013),and heavily polluted sea areas are particularly prone to harmful pathogens proliferation.These pathogens negatively impact seaweed growth,ultimately reducing laver yield and causing significant economic losses for local farmers.For instance,in 2004,approximately 5,000 hectares of N.yezoensis in the Nantong City maritime area suffered from severe rot,resulting in an estimated loss of 60 million RMB Yuan(Yangtze Evening Post,2004).Similarly,in 2016,over 1,300 hectares of N.yezoensis in the Rudong County maritime area of Nantong City experienced rot,with cost losses alone amounting to around 40 million RMB Yuan,causing economic losses to more than 3,000 laver farmers(Wang,2016).In January 2019,134 hectares of N.yezoensis in the Yancheng City maritime area exhibited rot,which was caused by the pathogenic bacterium Opliidopsis sp.(He et al.,2021).It should be clarified that seaweed cultivation inevitably faces diseases to varying degrees(Khan et al.,2024).These diseases encountered during laver cultivation are not unique to China but represent a global issue(Yang et al.,2020).For example,between 2013 and 2014,an outbreak of green spot disease in the laver farms in Sunchon,South Korea,could cause complete rot of laver thalli within 1-2 days,resulting in a loss of 1.1 million USD,equivalent to 10.7% of total farm sales(Kim et al.,2014).The sudden onset of such diseases during N.yezoensis cultivation often prevents timely and effective mitigation measures to reduce disease damage,ultimately leading to substantial losses for laver farmers.Neopyropia yezoensis cultivation demands high-quality seawater and thrives best in waters with moderate flow velocity and strong water exchange capacity(He et al.,2018).In Jiangsu Province,suitable cultivation areas have been largely exploited,limiting the potential for further expansion of the cultivation scale.Similarly,N.yezoensis struggles to grow in low-nutrient sea areas(Huang et al.,2023).Although the high levels of nitrogen and phosphorus in Jiangsu’s coastal waters support the growth of Neopyropia,the extensive cultivation area and high cultivation density inevitably restrict growth due to the limited carrying capacity of the sea area(Shan,2022).Taking the outer radial sandbars of Dafeng District in Yancheng City as an example,the laver cultivation scale once spanned a continuous distribution of 13,000 hectares.However,the excessive scale of cultivation adversely affected seawater exchange within the cultivation area(Shan,2022).As a result,laver in the center parts of the cultivation zone could not receive sufficient nutrient replenishment,leading to deficiencies essential for growth(Shan,2022).Additionally,the close proximity of cultivation facilities also facilitates the rapid spread of diseases,further reducing laver yields(Shan,2022).Concurrently,some marine areas in Jiangsu Province have been engaged in aquaculture activities that do not comply with regulations established by the Chinese government(Figure 2C).This noncompliance has exacerbated the scope and cultivation density of laver cultivation activities,creating additional challenges.Lin et al.(2021)identified two special utilization zones and six port shipping areas in Jiangsu Province where unreasonable or illegal laver cultivation activities occurred.These activities involved a total of 135.84 hectares,primarily concentrated in locations such as Tianwan Nuclear Power Plant Special Utilization Zone,Ganyu Port Special Utilization Zone,Shiqiao Port Shipping Area,Xuwei Port Shipping Area,Ganyu Port Shipping Area,Lvsi Port Shipping Area,Xiaomiao Hong Port Shipping Area,and Jinniu Port Shipping Area(Lin et al.,2021).Green seaweed blooms have persisted in the SYS for eighteen consecutive years(Zhang et al.,2019b;Xia et al.,2024b),predominantly caused by U.prolifera,which has led to significant adverse effects on marine aquaculture and related fisheries industries(Cao et al.,2023;Yao et al.,2024).On the one hand,the attachment of various Ulva species to laver cultivation facilities(Han et al.,2013;Huo et al.,2015)competes with Neopyropia for ecological niches and nutrients(Figure 2D),thereby impeding laver growth.On the other hand,removing attached green seaweeds during production incurs substantial labor costs for laver farmers(Sun et al.,2022a).Notably,the outbreak of large-scale green tide disasters near laver cultivation areas is rarely observed globally,with no similar reports from other countries or regions' laver cultivation areas.To effectively mitigate the scale of green tide outbreaks,the Ministry of Natural Resources of the People's Republic of China is currently focusing on reducing the biomass of U.prolifera attached to laver cultivation rafts in Jiangsu Province(Liu et al.,2021b;Xia et al.,2022;He et al.,2023;Sun et al.,2022b),and has taken measures to curb illegal occupation of marine areas for seaweed cultivation(Jiangsu Laver Association,2020).Additionally,laver farmers are encouraged to proactively adjust their raft cultivation schedules,including withdrawing facilities in advance during the production cycle and conducting early cleanup of green seaweeds(Figure 2E).These measures are aimed at maximizing ecological benefits(Sun et al.,2022a).However,these actions also impacted seaweed yields in Jiangsu Province,posing challenges to the long-term formation of a "common interest group" that balances fishery production and green tide control.For instance,in 2021,Jiangsu Province collectively retired approximately 4,000 hectares of laver cultivation and reduced the area of sea used for laver cultivation by about 6,400 hectares.By May 8,2021,all laver cultivation facilities were brought ashore,prematurely ending the laver production period spanned the late 2020 to mid-2021.This adjustment resulted in a revenue reduction of 1-1.2 billion RMB Yuan for the province's laver cultivation industry(Diao & Ma,2021)and led to widespread dissatisfaction among regional laver farmers about the potential economic impacts of green tide disaster management.Furthermore,since 2023,the funds allocated for green tide disaster prevention have nearly approached the actual direct economic benefits of laver cultivation in Jiangsu Province.Taking 2024 as a case in point,the annual investment in green tide prevention special funds(including both central and local government financial allocations)has exceeded one billion RMB Yuan,underscoring the financial burden of addressing this ecological challenge.The phenomenon of golden tide disasters impacting the laver cultivation industry is currently observed only in the marine regions of Jiangsu Province.The proliferation of Sargassum horneri,the primary species responsible for golden tides,has posed significant challenges to laver cultivation activities in Jiangsu Province in recent years.Since 2016,large-scale gatherings of drifting S.horneri have been frequently observed in the coastal waters off Jiangsu during winter and spring(Wang et al.,2023).The arrival of the golden tide "algal mat" in the laver raft cultivation area(Figure 2F)led to the structural collapse of some rafts(Zhuang et al.,2020).Moreover,golden tide seaweed entangled in the laver cultivation nets hinders Neopyropia from conducting photosynthesis effectively,leading to damage during its growth stage.To address this issue,laver farmers are compelled to manually remove S.horneri tangled around the rafts,which not only increases labor costs but also causes the detachment of Neopyropia during this process.Such disruptions often result in significant financial losses,amounting to hundreds of millions of RMB Yuan for local laver farmers(Liu et al.,2021c).For instance,from the winter of 2016 to the spring of 2017,the golden tide disaster severely impacted the laver cultivation industry in Jiangsu Province,causing economic losses of up to 500 million RMB Yuan in the laver cultivation industries of Yancheng and Nantong cities(Liu et al.,2018).Currently,there is no effective method to mitigate the golden tide macroalgal biomass at their source,as the origin of recent golden tide outbreaks in China remains unclear(Wang et al.,2024).Therefore,when laver cultivation activities are affected by golden tide disasters,manual clearance remains the only viable approach to minimize economic losses.Given the current climate warming trend,effective alleviation measures are challenging(Liu et al.,2021b).In areas where N.yezoensis is no longer suitable for growth,it could be worthwhile to gradually attempt the cultivation of heat-resistant strains,such as N.haitanensis(Zhou et al.,2023),which can contribute to the sustainable development of the laver cultivation industry in Jiangsu Province.Following the successful pilot cultivation of N.haitanensis in the SYS(Figure 2G),some laver farmers have opted to cease the cultivation of N.yezoensis in favor of N.haitanensis,while others have initiated experiments in the rotation planting of N.yezoensis and N.haitanensis.Taking 2024 as an example,Lianyun District People's Government of Lianyungang City has encouraged laver farmers to engage in the rotational cultivation of N.haitanensis and N.yezoensis(Liandao Subdistrict,2024).Laver farmers in Liandao Subdistrict have collectively piloted the cultivation of N.haitanensis over an area of approximately 800 hectares,achieving a bountiful harvest in October 2024,with an estimated annual yield of 15 tons per hectare(live weight),resulting in an annual output value of up to 130 million RMB Yuan(Liandao Subdistrict,2024).At present,the Jiangsu Provincial Government's promotion of the pilot rotational planting and cultivation scheme for N.yezoensis and N.haitanensis has achieved initial success and is deemed worthy of further promotion and application.At present,the Chinese government has focused on addressing the illegal occupation of maritime areas for aquaculture,explicitly prohibiting the establishment of new aquaculture projects that occupy natural coastlines or fall within ecological protection red lines(Ministry of Natural Resources of the People's Republic of China,2024).It has gradually cleared areas of illegal and unlicensed Neopyropia cultivation and withdrawn cultivation within the ecological red line areas(Figure 2C).Meanwhile,efforts are underway to optimize the ai_analysis.title_ko: 당혹감과 선택: 중국 장쑤성 김 양식업의 과제와 미래 발전
ai_analysis.abstract_ko: 해조류 양식은 식량 위기 해결과 탄소 흡수, 질소 순환 촉진, 부영양화 완화 등 생태적 편익을 제공하는 데 중요한 역할을 합니다. 전 세계적으로 아시아가 해조류 양식의 중심지이며, 중국이 가장 큰 비중을 차지하고 있습니다. 특히 중국 장쑤성 수베이 조간대는 세계 최대의 방사고려이지(방사탁, N. yezoensis) 양식지로, 지역 경제 발전과 빈곤 퇴치에 크게 기여해 왔습니다. 그러나 최근 장쑤성의 김 양식 산업은 여러 가지 도전에 직면해 있습니다.
summary_3lines: 중국 장쑤성 조간대의 대규모 김 양식 산업 현황과 그 기여도를 분석하고 직면한 과제를 파악하고자 했다.
50년간 발전해온 장쑤성 김 양식업이 세계 최대 규모로 성장했으나, 최근 다양한 환경적·구조적 도전에 직면하고 있음을 밝혔다.
해조류 양식의 지속 가능한 발전을 위해 연안 생태계 보호와 조화로운 양식업 관리 방안 마련의 시사점을 도출했다.
ai_analysis.research_purpose: 중국 장쑤성 조간대에서 50년 이상 지속되어 온 대규모 김 양식 산업의 발전 과정과 경제·생태적 기여도를 평가하고, 최근 직면한 과제들을 분석하여 향후 지속 가능한 발전 방향을 모색하는 것을 목적으로 한다.
key_findings: 중국은 전 세계 해조류 생산량의 약 60%를 차지하는 최대 생산국이다.
장쑤성 수베이 조간대는 2023년 기준 전국 김 양식 면적의 51.81%를 차지하는 세계 최대의 방사고려이지 양식지이다.
김 양식업은 연안 지역 경제 성장과 빈곤 퇴치에 크게 기여해왔으나 현재 다양한 과제에 직면해 있다.
practical_applications: 해상 양식장이 국립공원 해양 생태계 및 경관에 미치는 영향을 주기적으로 모니터링한다.
국립공원 인근 해역의 양식 활동과 해양 생태계 보전이 공존할 수 있는 관리 지침을 수립한다.
연안 지역주민과의 협력을 통해 친환경 양식 기법 도입을 유도하고 해양 오염원을 저감한다.
ai_analysis.korea_np_applicability_reason: 한국 국립공원 내에도 해상 양식장이 일부 존재하나, 본 논문은 중국의 대규모 상업적 양식업에 초점을 맞추고 있어 국내 국립공원 현장에는 직접적인 양식 기술보다 해양 생태계 관리 및 지역사회 상생 관점에서 제한적으로 참고할 수 있다.
related_laws: 야생생물 보호 및 관리에 관한 법률 제8조
field_checklist: 국립공원 구역 내 불법 양식 시설물 존재 여부 확인
해양 양식 활동으로 인한 인근 해양 보호생물 서식지 훼손 여부 점검
양식업 폐기물(그물, 부자 등)의 해안가 방치 상태 조사
수질 오염 및 부영양화 관련 해양 환경 모니터링 실시
공원 내 어민 및 양식업 종사자 대상 친환경 관리 안내 이행 여부 확인
cautions: 해외 대규모 상업 양식 모델을 국내 국립공원의 엄격한 보전 지구에 직접 적용하는 것은 부적절하다.
어민 생계와 공원 보전 간의 갈등이 발생할 수 있으므로 현장 적용 시 신중한 접근이 필요하다.

papers.title: Synthetic Biology and Endangered Species
papers.abstract: Ecologists warn of an ongoing extinction crisis. More than 1 million species are at risk of extinction, and millions more are in dangerous decline. Ecosystems under accelerating stress—such as some coral reefs—from climate change and other impacts could disappear within decades. Now a growing number of conservation scientists, conservation organizations, government agencies, and ethicists are debating the potential benefits and dangers of synthetic biology (tools and methods applied at the genetic scale) to help species and habitats survive human-driven onslaughts. Synthetic biology is rewriting the rules of nature with advances in genetic engineering, gene editing, and gene drives (an inheritable form of gene editing). For decades, agricultural technology companies have developed and implemented genetic tools to control pests and improve crops and domesticated animals. Now, conservation science has test cases as well. A genetically engineered American chestnut tree (Castanea dentata) is growing in research fields in New York State. A wheat-derived single strand of DNA has been added to the tree's 40,000 genes, blocking a fatal acid produced by an invasive fungus (Cryphonectria parasitica). This tree is the first transgenic organism in the pipeline for regulatory approval in the United States with a conservation goal. But opponents argue that a transgenic tree in the wild could have unknown effects on forest ecosystems. Scientists are also testing cloning technologies to revive a rare species. In 2021, a black-footed ferret (Mustela nigripes) was successfully cloned. She will be partnered with a captive black-footed ferret. The goal is to increase genetic fitness and improve reproduction rates among captive and reintroduced black-footed ferret populations. These black-footed ferret kits were raised at the National Black-Footed Ferret Conservation Center in Colorado so that they could be reintroduced into the wild. Photograph: Kimberly Fraser/US Fish and Wildlife Service, CC BY-SA 2.0. The tools and methods of synthetic biology could be the future of a new precision conservation. These biotechnologies could offer scientists unprecedented accuracy, speed, and efficiency to help species adapt to disrupted habitats and control invasive pests and pathogens. Conservation biotechnology is an extension of what humans have done for thousands of years—though far more aggressively in recent decades—in shaping the evolution of wild and domesticated species. Humans must take the reins of nature more firmly in hand so that threatened species and ecosystems can survive, according to Beth Shapiro, a paleogeneticist at the University of California, Santa Cruz. “Disagreement about whether biodiversity would be better served by leaving nature alone or intervening more aggressively has deep roots in biodiversity conservation,” Shapiro writes in her 2021 book Life as We Made It: How 50,000 Years of Human Innovation Refined—and Redefined—Nature. But there “are those of us who believe that it is too late to imagine any portion of the planet not impacted by us, and instead, we must embrace our role as planetary curators.” Critics, though, say that humans are going too far, that science should not interfere so deeply in nature. Wildlife and their habitats are immensely complex. Synthetic biology could lead to disastrous unintended consequences. Synbio (synthetic biological) species or their offspring, therefore, should not be allowed in natural places, even if the goal is to save them, these critics say. Allowing biotech life into the wild could threaten how conservationists and the public think about nature, according to Eric Katz, retired professor of philosophy from the New Jersey Institute of Technology and a distinguished senior fellow at the Institute for Philosophy and Public Policy at George Mason University. Conservationists have long argued that natural places are fundamentally different from domesticated and other human-dominated ones. Wild places where cloned or artificially modified species are inserted would no longer be considered natural and could lose the special status that protects them. Conservation biotech is blurring language long used to encourage or justify saving wild species and ecosystems, argues Katz. “It could change the very meaning of nature and conservation and preservation,” he says. “If science and tech can create anything we want, what is the purpose of traditional conservation and preservation practices?” Over the first four decades of the twentieth century, an estimated 4 billion American chestnut trees died across their range from Maine to Mississippi. Their killer was a pathogen accidentally introduced in shipments of Chinese chestnut (Castanea mollissima), an ornamental tree that had evolved blight protection. American chestnuts were once giants, rising 80–100 feet, with massive trunks. It was a key species in the ecology of North American forests. In some forests, American chestnuts were responsible for up to 45% of the canopy. The annual fall of nutritious nuts was a crucial food source for Indigenous peoples. Today, the American chestnut is functionally extinct, and most survivors are stunted, rising only about 15 feet, and unable to bear fruit. Once ranging from Maine to Mississippi, the American chestnut was a key forest species felled by an invasive fungus, but scientists are exploring genetic engineering and other techniques to restore it. Photograph: The American Chestnut Foundation. Scientists first tried to bring back American chestnuts by crossing them with blight-resistant Chinese chestnuts, but that did not result in a thriving hybrid. Other techniques to bring back the American chestnut were considered too slow or ineffective. But researchers finally identified a possible solution, inserting blight-fighting DNA from wheat into American chestnuts. The project is led by William Powell, director of the American Chestnut Research and Restoration Project at the State University of New York College of Environmental Science and Forestry (ESF). These American chestnut trees—known as Darling 58—have been planted in regulated fields. To strengthen Darling trees, Powell's lab and The American Chestnut Foundation (TACF) have crossed them with wild American chestnuts. By 2023, the Darling tree could be fully approved by the Environmental Protection Agency, the US Department of Agriculture, and, because the nut is a food, the Food and Drug Administration. Restoring the American chestnut to its original range would require public and private mobilizations to plant, propagate, and maintain millions of transgenic seedlings. But that process is many years away. If approved, Darling trees will be distributed to long-term research plots and relatively small-scale public horticultural sites. Plantings will be monitored by citizen scientists under guidance of TACF, a nonprofit organization that supports and partners the restoration. Later, Darling trees would be distributed to the wider public. In 2021, the National Association of State Foresters declared its support for genetically modifying native trees to fight off destructive invasive pests if conventional measures fail. Numerous groups and individuals have asked for transgenic chestnut seedlings to plant, including the Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians in North Carolina, which is exploring cultivation of them on tribal land. Other native communities have given similar nods to the Darling tree. The Sierra Club has offered its blessing, but only if Indigenous people continue to support it. Students at SUNY's College of Environmental Science and Forestry perform stem inoculations on young transgenic American chestnut trees to test if they show enhanced resistance to the blight fungus. Photograph: The American Chestnut Foundation. An American chestnut in Kentucky towers over a man. While these trees have been functionally gone from forests for nearly a century, some isolated mature ones have survived. Photograph: The American Chestnut Foundation. But some environmental activists are opposed. Ann Petermann, director of the Global Justice Ecology Project, a US-based environmental organization, says that it is wrong to alter the gene pool of wild trees. “We could be looking at forests that aren't natural or wild but filled with genetically engineered versions of formerly wild trees.” The Darling tree is not a moneymaker; there are no plans to patent it. But the transgenic chestnut project is being used by industry as a Trojan horse, allowing corporations to gain broader public acceptance of transgenic forestry products, according to Petermann. If transgenic American chestnuts are growing wild in forests, Petermann says, regulators could be more likely to approve genetically engineered trees for commercial uses such as hybrid poplar cultivars in field trials supported by industry. Leading companies in commercial forestry do support the Darling project, among them Bayer (formerly Monsanto) and ArborGen, which are among the largest suppliers of pine seedlings for forestry projects in the United States. Critics of Darling trees worry about their potential negative impacts on native plants, animals, and microbes. Tests by ESF researchers and collaborators on Darling trees, however, have found no harm to native frogs, insects, or germination of other trees’ seeds. Independent tests have not found nutritional differences in transgenic nuts that could harm wildlife or humans. Reviving the American chestnut could have benefits for pollinators, stream invertebrates, and wildlife consumers of nuts. During the spring breeding season of 2022, the cloned black-footed ferret named Elizabeth Ann was expected to pair up with an experienced suitor in a conservation center outside of Fort Collins, Colorado. Choosing the right mate was important. The black-footed ferret is perhaps the rarest mammal in North America, and Elizabeth Ann is far too valuable to risk injury from an aggressive male. In the 1970s, scientists thought the black-footed ferret was extinct in the wild. In 1981, however, a colony of survivors was discovered. The little colony thrived for a while before sylvatic plague, caused by the same bacterium that causes plague in humans, decimated the population. The US Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS) captured the surviving 18 ferrets for a captive breeding program. Only seven of those animals managed to reproduce. Today, about 250–350 ferrets live in captivity, and 300 more live on reintroduction sites in the wild—all descended from the seven founders, except for Elizabeth Ann. The cloning of Elizabeth Ann is the brainchild of Revive & Restore, a biotech conservation organization based in Sausalito, California. In 2012, the futurist Stewart Brand and his wife, Ryan Phelan, created Revive & Restore to support research on advanced technologies that could be used to protect endangered species and perhaps revive extinct species. In 2018, the organization and its partners received a first-of-its-kind endangered species recovery permit from the USFWS to attempt a genetic rescue of the black-footed ferret. Elizabeth Ann, the first cloned US endangered species, is a black-footed ferret, although her siblings and surrogate mother are domestic ferrets. Photograph (left): US Fish and Wildlife Service National Black-footed Ferret Conservation Center. Photograph (right) Cassie, with the USFWS National Black-footed Ferret Conservation Center. Elizabeth Ann is a genetic replica of a black-footed ferret named Willa that died in captivity 35 years ago and never reproduced. Willa was a surviving member of a lost colony of a different lineage than the founders. Fortunately, a cell culture from Willa's tissues had been stored in a freezer. Decades later, embryos were created from that cell culture and implanted in three domestic ferrets (Mustela putorius). One surrogate mother gave birth to Elizabeth Ann. The ferret cloning was done by a consortium that included the USFWS, ViaGen (a Texas-based pet and horse cloning company), Revive & Restore, the Association of Zoos and Aquariums, and the San Diego Zoo. Elizabeth Ann is the first native endangered animal species in North America to be cloned—and the first to reach sexual maturity. If Elizabeth Ann breeds in captivity, she could introduce her much-needed genetic fitness into the remnant population. But was creating Elizabeth Ann the right thing to do? “You can do genetic cloning,” says Samantha Wisely, a conservation geneticist at the University of Florida and a consultant on the Elizabeth Ann cloning project. “But should you do genetic cloning? Every incorporation of new biotechnology into conservation should have that question asked.” Wisely collaborated on a 2021 study in Biological Conservation on the ethics of the black-footed ferret cloning project with Ronald Sandler, a philosopher and director of Northeastern University's Ethics Institute. The team asked questions such as whether cloning was the best tool available for a conservation purpose, whether it could be done responsibly in this case, and whether there was support from the public and within the conservation community for the project. “New technologies are moving forward in a lot of different ways in lots of different spaces,” says Sandler. “The question is whether there is an ability to make good decisions about which technologies, in what context, and under what conditions they should be used. We should look not only at how the technologies work but also at things like who controls them, who shoulders the costs, and who are the beneficiaries.” Cloning, for instance, was not only the best tool in this situation but the only tool available to introduce genetic fitness into the endangered population, according to Wisely. There were no other individuals to add to the genetic pool beyond the original seven founders. Sandler and his colleagues concluded that the cloning project was done responsibly. “The partners have a track record of thinking through issues in a thoughtful, collaborative way,” he says. “The initial point of the project isn't to modify the ferrets; it's just to increase the genetic diversity of the population in the context of a captive breeding and release program. So this project fits into the standard, familiar conservation practices and paradigms.” The Sandler team did recommend that the cloning project should more fully inform local landowners and other stakeholders about its progress. But what makes the Elizabeth Ann project important is not just that she is the first clone of an endangered species native to North America. It is that cloning could make other powerful technologies more feasible as the logical next step in restoring wild populations of the black-footed ferret. Those technologies would almost certainly be more controversial than cloning because they would alter the genome of the animal instead of duplicating it. Elizabeth Ann lacks a critical feature that her progeny would need in the wild. Now Revive & Restore researchers and partners are exploring the use of CRISPR and other advanced tools to immunize black-footed ferrets and future generations against sylvatic plague, the invasive pathogen from Europe that infects their primary food source, the prairie dog. The domestic ferret, originally from Europe, has developed natural immunity to the plague. Researchers hope to identify DNA in domestic ferrets that codes for immunity. If that is successful, scientists might be able to CRISPR edit immunizing DNA into the population of black-footed ferrets. CRISPR is a gene-modifying suite of techniques. (The acronym stands for clustered regularly interspaced palindromic repeats.) CRISPR is the fastest, most inexpensive, and most precise way to manipulate the code of life. ai_analysis.title_ko: 합성생물학과 멸종위기종
ai_analysis.abstract_ko: 생태학자들은 현재 진행 중인 대멸종 위기에 대해 경고하고 있다. 100만 종 이상의 생물이 멸종 위기에 처해 있으며, 수백만 종이 위험한 감소 추세를 보이고 있다. 기후변화 및 기타 영향으로 가속화되는 스트레스를 받는 생태계(예: 일부 산호초)는 수십 년 안에 사라질 수 있다. 이제 점점 더 많은 보전 과학자, 보전 단체, 정부 기관, 윤리학자들이 인간이 주도하는 파괴로부터 종과 서식지가 생존할 수 있도록 돕기 위해 합성생물학(유전체 수준에서 적용되는 도구와 방법)의 잠재적 이익과 위험성을 논의하고 있다. 합성생물학은 유전공학, 유전자 편집, 유전자 드라이브(유전 가능한 형태의 유전자 편집)의 발전과 함께 자연의 규칙을 다시 쓰고 있다. 수십 년 동안 농업 기술 기업들은 해충을 방제하고 작물과 가축을 개량하기 위해 유전적 도구를 개발하고 적용해 왔다. 이제 보전 과학에도 실증 사례가 생겼다. 유전자 조작된 미국밤나무(Castanea dentata)가 뉴욕주의 연구 전에서 자라고 있다. 밀에서 유래한 단일 가닥 DNA가 이 나무의 4만 개 유전자에 추가되어 침입성 진균(Cryphonectria parasitica)이 생성하는 치명적인 산을 차단한다. 이 나무는 미국에서 보전 목적의 규제 승인을 앞둔 최초의 형질전환 유기체이다. 그러나 반대론자들은 야생의 형질전환 나무가 숲 생태계에 알 수 없는 영향을 미칠 수 있다고 주장한다. 과학자들은 또한 희귀종을 부활시키기 위해 복제 기술을 테스트하고 있다. 2021년, 검은발족제비(Mustela nigripes)가 성공적으로 복제되었다. 이 암컷은 사육 중인 검은발족제비와 짝을 이룰 것이다. 목표는 사육 및 재 도입된 검은발족제비 개체군의 유전적 건강을 높이고 번식률을 향상시키는 것이다. 이 검은발족제비 새끼들은 콜로라도에 있는 국립 검은발족제비 보전 센터에서 사육되어 야생에 재도입될 수 있도록 했다. 합성생물학의 도구와 방법은 새로운 정밀 보전의 미래가 될 수 있다. 이러한 생명공학은 과학자들에게 파괴된 서식지에 종이 적응하고 침입성 해충과 병원체를 제어할 수 있도록 전례 없는 정확성, 속도, 효율성을 제공할 수 있다.
summary_3lines: 기후변화와 서식지 파괴로 인한 멸종위기종 증가에 대응하여 유전공학 등 합성생물학 기술의 보전 목적 활용 가능성과 쟁점을 분석함.
미국밤나무 유전자 조작 및 검은발족제비 복제 등 최신 생명공학 기술을 활용한 멸종위기종 회복 사례를 조사함.
정밀 보전을 위한 생명공학 도입은 생태계 적응력을 높일 수 있으나 생태계 교란 등의 잠재적 위험에 대한 신중한 접근이 요구됨.
ai_analysis.research_purpose: 본 연구는 심각해지는 기후변화와 생물다양성 위기 속에서 유전공학, 유전자 편집, 복제 등 합성생물학 기술이 멸종위기종 보전과 서식지 복원에 어떻게 적용될 수 있는지 그 가능성과 한계를 검토하고자 한다.
key_findings: 침입성 진균에 저항성을 갖도록 유전자 조작된 미국밤나무가 보전 목적의 규제 승인을 앞두고 있음
2021년 멸종위기종인 검은발족제비의 성공적 복제를 통해 유전적 다양성 회복과 번식률 제고의 기반을 마련함
합성생물학은 종과 서식지의 생존을 돕는 정밀 보전의 도구가 될 수 있으나, 생태계 교란 우려에 대한 논쟁이 지속됨
practical_applications: 기후변화와 외래유입 병원체로 고사 위기에 처한 공원 내 특산·멸종위기 식물(예: 구상나무)에 대한 유전적 모니터링 및 보전 대책 수립에 참고
국내 고유 멸종위기 야생생물 복원 사업 시, 전통적 증식 방식을 넘어선 유전적 다양성 분석 및 관리 기법 도입 검토
생명공학 기술 적용에 따른 생태계 교란 가능성을 사전에 검증할 수 있는 환경영향평가 및 모니터링 지침 마련
ai_analysis.korea_np_applicability_reason: 한국 국립공원에서도 기후변화로 인한 구상나무 등 멸종위기종 쇠퇴 문제가 심각하나, 유전자 조작이나 복제와 같은 합성생물학 기술은 엄격한 법적 규제와 자연성 보존 원칙으로 인해 현장 적용보다는 장기적 연구 및 모니터링 관점에서 제한적으로 다루어짐
related_laws: 야생생물 보호 및 관리에 관한 법률 제12조
field_checklist: 공원 내 기후변화 취약 식물종(구상나무 등)의 쇠퇴 및 고사 현황 파악 여부
멸종위기 야생생물 복원 개체군의 유전적 다양성(근친교배 등) 저하 여부 확인
외래 병해충 및 침입성 유기체로 인한 생태계 피해 모니터링 실시 여부
유전자원 채취 및 연구 목적의 출입 시 관련 법령에 따른 허가 절차 준수 여부
신기술 도입에 따른 생태계 교란 가능성에 대한 사전 전문가 자문 실시 여부
cautions: 유전자 조작이나 생물 복원 기술은 생태계 교란 및 윤리적 논란의 소지가 크므로 국내 법령 및 정책 기조에 맞춰 신중하게 접근해야 함
